metadata.sections: 3.9 ADA – Selection of Actions for Action Groups

content:
The table defines how individual “load cases” are identified, classified and combined for structural analysis (e.g. in a RAG-based vector store context).  It consists essentially of two columns—Item and Description—with an implicit context of “ACT” (action), “LC” (load case), and “SUP” (superposition settings).  Below is a detailed breakdown of each Item:

1. NO  
   • Purpose: Selects which load case(s) to include.  
   • Values:  
     – Positive integer n (>0): only load case number n.  
     – 0: all load cases belonging to the currently defined action.  
     – –1: all load cases belonging to the currently defined category.

2. TYPE  
   • Purpose: Defines the broad load type.  
   • Typical codes:  
     – G or PERM: “Always (permanent)” loads.  Applied with a permanent (γG) partial‐safety factor that comes from the ACT-item’s SUP record.  

3. PERC  
   • Code: “Always (permanent), however with variable factors.”  
   • Behavior: Treated like a permanent action, but partial‐safety factors can vary per load case. These factors are drawn from the SUP record of the associated ACT item.

4. Q  
   • Code: “Conditional” (sometimes also marked P).  
   • Behavior: Only unfavourable (worst‐case) effects are considered.  The partial‐safety factor is taken from the SUP record for conditionally unfavorable actions.

5. W  
   • Code: “Alternating” load case.  
   • Behavior: Both positive and negative load phases may act unfavourably (e.g. seismic or fatigue).  The SUP record entry “UNSI” governs the unfavourable side.

6. F  
   • Code: “Follow-up.”  
   • Behavior: Added on top of a primary load case but only if that primary case is active in superposition.  Enables capturing sequential or secondary effects.

7. AG1 … AG99  
   • Codes: Permanent alternative load case groups, numbered 1 through 99.  
   • Behavior:  
     – “Permanent alternative” means one and only one group of these cases may apply within the same action (mutually exclusive).  
     – If you assign AGk to multiple load cases, the solver will choose the worst combination among them—but never combine two from the same group.  
     – Can also be used multiplicatively: the initial load case factor is multiplied rather than simply added.

Additional notes on usage:  
• By mixing NO, TYPE, PERC, Q, W, F and AG-groups in a single superposition definition (LC), you can build virtually any combination of loads—constant, slowly varying, alternating, conditional or follow-up.  
• You may reuse the same “load case” number across different types (e.g. once as TYPE=G and again as TYPE=Q), allowing “unit load cases” to perform influence-line or modal analyses within a general static framework.  
• When defining a superposition (LC record), you can reference individual or grouped cases, or even load case sets that were pre-combined elsewhere in the model.  

This table thus provides a flexible schema to tag and combine structural load cases, ensure correct application of partial-safety factors, respect exclusivity rules, and capture secondary or alternating load effects.

Below is a self-contained, field-by-field description of the “LC” superposition record as it appears in your table, augmented with the context you provided. It covers all input fields, their codes, meanings, units and defaults.

1. Record name: LC  
   Purpose: Defines one load case (or a group of load cases) to be included in a superposition analysis. You can repeat the LC record for different combinations or reuse the same load case in multiple types.

2. Fields

  • NO  
    – Description: Load-case identifier.  
      • A nonnegative integer (e.g. 1,2,3…) selects exactly that numbered load case from the database.  
      • 0 means “all load cases belonging to the current action.”  
      • –1 means “all load cases belonging to the current category.”  
    – Unit: –  
    – Default: (must be specified)

  • TYPE  
    – Description: Selects the type of action and partial-safety treatment. The codes map to the ACT → TYPE item in your action definitions.  
      • G or PERM   : Permanent (always) loads, partial-safety factor applied action-wise.  
      • PERC       : Permanent loads with variable factors, partial-safety factor applied load-case-wise.  
      • Q or COND   : Conditional loads (only the unfavourable sign is taken into account).  
      • W or UNSI   : Alternating loads (both positive and negative values are considered if unfavourable, e.g. seismic).  
      • F           : Follow-up load case (added to the previous main case only if that case is active in the superposition).  
    – Unit: –  
    – Default: PERM

  • SUP  
    – Description: Alternative/exclusive group designation. This code controls how multiple load cases interact in superposition (i.e. “only one of these may act,” or “sign shall be inverted,” etc.). The SUP codes correspond to ACT → SUP in the action definition.  
    – Allowed values:  
      * ALEX      : Alias for AG1 (see below). Pulled from ACT → SUP if you set SUP=AG1 there.  
      * A1 … A99  : Alternative permanent load-case groups 1 through 99. All in one group are treated as mutually exclusive—only the worst-case member is taken.  
      * EXCL      : Alias for a generic “exclusive” group (similar to A1) as defined in ACT → SUP.  
      * X1 … X99  : Alternative groups 1 through 99, but with changing sign. In each group only one load case acts, and its sign is flipped if that gives a worse effect.  
      * USEX      : A further alias you may define in ACT → SUP for exclusive grouping.  
    – Notes:  
      • If SUP is omitted, AG1 is assumed.  
      • For non‐linear load cases only AG1 (the default group) is permitted.  
    – Unit: –  
    – Default: AG1

  • FACT  
    – Description: Multiplication factor applied to the internal forces or displacements of the selected load case before adding it into the superposition. You can use this to scale unit loads, impose dynamic factors, etc.  
    – Unit: – (dimensionless; denoted “– / LIT” in the table)  
    – Default: 1.0

3. Usage notes  
  – You may define any combination of LC records to assemble complex load patterns: different actions, different groups, conditional and alternating loads.  
  – Because each LC can be reused under different TYPE and SUP settings, you can build up all required design cases by repeating only those load cases that actually differ in type, sign or group.  
  – In purely linear (static) analyses you can even treat each LC as a unit load case, multiply it by FACT, and then superpose—all within one run.

See also: ACT

TYPE PERM The decision whether all load cases of one permanent action with PART G or P are taken into account as favourable or unfavourable is effected by determination of sums. It means that either the favourable or unfavourable factor is used for all load cases..

 A mixing of load case with TYPE PERC and other types (PERM, ALEX) is not recommended. In this case, the load cases should be assigned to different permanent actions.
 More explanations and an example for PERM and PERC is available at
 https://www.sofistik.de/documentation/2025/en/tutorials/superpositions/action-g-lc-perm-perc/ superposition_action-G-lc-perm-perc.html
 Differentiation of TYPE AG1-AG99 and A1-A99
 TYPE AG1-AG99 The most unfavourable load case of a permanent alternative load case group within one action is determined and added. But one load case is used always for each alternative group per one action.
 TYPE A1-A99 The most unfavourable load case of the alternative load case group within one action is determined and it is only added, if it acts un- favourably.
 More explanations and an example for the alternative load case groups available at
 https://www.sofistik.de/documentation/2025/en/tutorials/superpositions/ action-sup-alex-excl-exex/superposition_action-sup-alex-excl-exex.html
 Consideration of load cases with TYPE AG1-AG99 or ALEX, if they are a part of a permanent action e.g. G:
 For load cases, which have the TYPE AG1-AG99 or ALEX and which are a part of a permanent action and its categories, the sum of all values of the permanent action is decisive whether the load cases are favourable or unfavourable. This is the same procedure as for TYPE PERM.
 Follow-up load case F
 If a follow-up load case is defined, it is considered only, if the relevant main load case has a part for the superposition.

content:
For load cases, which have the TYPE AG1-AG99 or ALEX and which are a part of a permanent action and its categories, the sum of all values of the permanent action is decisive whether the load cases are favourable or unfavourable. This is the same procedure as for TYPE PERM.. Follow-up load case F. If a follow-up load case is defined, it is considered only, if the relevant main load case has a part for the superposition..
 Example:
 ACT W $variable action wind$ LC 11 TYP A1 $main load case$ LC 12 TYP F $follow-up load case$
 If the load case 11 of the variable action W acts favourably and thus it does not have a part for the superposition, then also the load case 12 is not considered.
 Default for TYPE:
 The default depends on the default superposition of the load cases (SUP), which is input with record ACT. All superpositions SUP PERM get the TYPE G, all superpositions SUP COND get the TYPE Q, all superpositions SUP EXCL get the TYPE A1 ..., all superpositions SUP UNSI get the type W, all superpositions SUP USEX get the TYPE X1.... and all superpositions SUP ALEX get the TYPE AG1. SUP PERC of the record ACT corresponds to TYPE PERC. Modifications of the types are only temporarily processed in MAXIMA. That means these inputs are only considered in this MAXIMA calculation. The default from record ACT SUP is overlaid then! In case of doubt it is recommended to use the default from record ACT and not input a literal for TYPE at LC.
 The default for the input with the standard combination (COMB EXTR STAN) is for TYPE as follows:
 load case 1: G
 all other load cases: Q
 Among the load cases of an alternative load case group, only the one with the most detrimental effect is used for a superposition. The load case with the most detrimental effect among the groups A1 to A99, X1 to X99 is handled as a live load, i.e. if none of the load cases has a detrimental effect, these groups are not taken into consideration at all. However, one load case is always considered for the permanent alternative load case groups AG1 to AG99. The as- signment of the alternative groups to one or more ACT records is decisive for the superposition result.
 The superposition of non-linearly analysed load cases is only permitted, if they are superim- posed using TYPE AG1 without the ACT record. If using the literal NONL for EXTR in record COMB, the load cases are processed automatically with TYPE AG1. Then the program cal- culates the effective load case as a selection from a series of non-linear analyses (extreme values boundary lines).

content: Using FACT, an additional factor can be defined for the initial load cases, with which the cor- responding internal force (value to be superimposed) is multiplied. The multiplication with the factor is done before the actual superposition. This is important, if a negative factor (e.g. -1.0) is used. In this case the load cases which initially supply an unfavourable contribution are used then as favourable for the superposition and vice versa.

The input table defines two related parameter groups—COMB (combination rule) and ETYP (element type)—each with its valid options, units and defaults.  It is typically used together with other control keywords (ECHO, CTRL, ACT, ADD, LC, SUPP, SLVL) to drive selective result superposition and extraction in a structural‐analysis environment.

1. Table Structure  
   • Columns  
     – Item: keyword or sub‐keyword name.  
     – Description: what the parameter controls and any special notes.  
     – Unit: either a unit symbol (e.g. “LIT” for literal values) or “—” when unitless.  
     – Default: the value assumed if none is supplied.  

2. Parameter Group: COMB  
   (Controls the definition and numbering of superposition rules and the extreme‐value logic.)

   • COMB  
     – Description: Integer index of the combination rule under which results will be superposed. Each distinct COMB value identifies one rule.  
     – Unit: — (unitless integer).  
     – Default: 1.

   • EXTR  
     – Description: Specifies how the program computes “extreme” results when superposing multiple load‐case results under a given COMB rule.  
     – Unit: LIT (literal text).  
     – Default: MAMI.  
     – Valid values:  
       • MAX  → Determine only maximum values across the selected load cases.  
       • MIN  → Determine only minimum values.  
       • MAMI → Compute both MAX and MIN envelopes.  
       • SRSS → Square‐root‐sum‐of‐squares combination (no sign information).  
       • SRSE → Signed SRSS: takes the root‐sum‐of‐squares but retains the overall sign of the resulting extreme.

3. Parameter Group: ETYP  
   (Selects which element types or result‐sets are included in extraction or superposition.)

   • ETYP  
     – Description: Literal token selecting the element type(s) for which results are to be generated or combined.  
     – Unit: LIT.  
     – Default: AUTO.  
     – Valid values:  
       • AUTO → Automatically include all element types present in the model.  
       • NODE → Nodal points (displacements, forces at nodes).  
       • SPAC → Nodal accelerations and velocities.  
       • BOUN → Individual boundary‐element results.  
       • BOUS → Sum results of boundary elements.  
       • BEAM → Beam‐element internal forces/moments.  
       • DSLN → Design elements.  
       • BSCT → External beam sections (imported from SIR).  
       • TRUS → Truss elements.  
       • CABL → Cables.  
       • SPRI → Springs.  
       • CFM  → Kinematic constraint elements.  
       • QUAD → Plane (2D) elements.  
       • QNOD → Node results of plane elements.  
       • QBED → Bedding (foundation) of plane elements.  
       • BRIC → Volume (3D) elements.  
       • BNOD → Node results of volume elements.  
       • RSET → Predefined result set.  
       • SLVL → Storey‐level results.  

4. Usage Notes  
   – COMB and EXTR are typically used in conjunction with the SUPP keyword to pick and weight specific load-case results for the named combination rule.  
   – ETYP allows you to restrict post‐processing to only certain types of model entities (e.g. beams or shells).  
   – When defining a new COMB rule, you supply a unique COMB number and then list one or more SUPP lines referencing load cases and their factors. EXTR then governs how those factors combine to produce an envelope, SRSS, etc.  
   – The designation field (e.g. for a superposition case title) is limited to 18 characters of user text—program prefixes consume an additional 14 characters internally to store element type and rule info.  

By capturing COMB, EXTR and ETYP in your RAG‐vector store, you can retrieve and reconstruct precisely which combination rule was applied, how extremes were computed, and on which element classes the results were generated.

Below is a comprehensive description of the input table used to define scalar variables or objective functions for “selective superposition” in the RAG vector‐store workflow. Wherever helpful, we refer to related constructs (ECHO, CTRL, COMB, ACT, ADD, LC) or to table footnotes.  

1. SUPP (Superposition Specification)  
   • Purpose: identifies which load cases or element subsets enter the superposition sum.  
   • Relationship: works in tandem with OPT = S (see below) to pick out only those elements defined by the FROM, TO, INC range.  

2. SLVL (Storey Results)  
   • Not explicitly parameterized here, but typically signals that the output will be organized by “storey” or level in a building model.  

3. TYPE  
   • Two alternatives:  
     – Scalar variable: direct extraction of a single value (e.g. maximum axial force in a beam).  
     – Objective function: a user-defined combination of scalar variables (see “Objective function” explanations elsewhere).  

4. LT (Literal Tag)  
   • AUTO: Default tag that tells the program to collect “all scalar variables available for the selected element types.”  
   • If overridden, LT can carry a user-supplied label identifying a specific output quantity or function.  

5. Item Description / Unit / Default  
   • Provides a short label, physical unit, and default setting for each selected scalar.  
   • By default (AUTO), the system enumerates every applicable scalar (e.g. displacements, forces, stresses) for the chosen elements.  

6. FROM / TO / INC  
   • Defines a numeric range (or group) of elements over which you want the scalar or objective to be reported.  
     – FROM: starting index, group name, or secondary-group identifier (for ETYP = BEAM, TRUS, CABL, BOUN or SAR only).  
     – TO: ending index, group or SLN/SAR number, or SLN identifier.  
     – INC: step size (increment). Must be positive; “*” can be used to signal default automatic stepping.  
   • Special case for BEAM elements: INC can be “X” plus a value in [m], or a normalized fraction [–] between 0 (start) and 1 (end), or percentages [%] or per-thousand [‰].  
   • SELE (Selection code) may substitute for FROM/TO/INC if you’re picking specific nodes (QNOD, BNOD) or cross‐section points (BEAM, DSLN).  

7. LC (Load Case)  
   • The first saved load case number that participates in this superposition. Subsequent load cases can be added via SUPP entries.  

8. TITL (Title)  
   • User’s designation for the newly generated superposed load case or combined result.  
   • Up to 32 characters may be entered, but only 18 appear explicitly:  
     – The program reserves 9 characters for “superposition info” and 5 for “element-type code” at the start.  
   • Once saved in the database during the first run, this title persists—even if you modify the SUPP definitions later.  

9. OPT (Options)  
   • Only valid literal value: “S” (Selective superposition).  
   • When OPT = S, the engine sums only those element results falling inside the specified FROM–TO–INC range. SUPP lines then list exactly which original load cases (and multipliers) to combine.  

Usage Notes  
• The combination of TYPE = scalar or objective, OPT = S, and a properly defined FROM–TO–INC block lets you extract exactly those internal forces, displacements, or custom functions for a user-defined subset of elements or beam sections.  
• SUPP entries following this header carry two critical pieces of information: the load case number and its superposition coefficient (positive, negative, or zero).  
• Because TITL is immortalized on first write, change carefully: if you need a different label, create a new superposition set rather than overwriting.  

Cross-References  
• ECHO / CTRL: control global output verbosity and saving options.  
• COMB / ACT: higher-level commands to assemble multiple SUPP definitions into a single actionable combination.  
• ADD / LC: add new load cases or fetch existing ones for use in SUPP.

See also: ECHO, CTRL, COMB, ACT, ADD, LC

The table is a reference key for all “TYPE” codes that can be requested when extracting superposition factors of support reactions, nodal displacements and rotations in MAXIMA (the post-processing module). It ties together four pieces of information for each code:

1. TYPE code  
2. Human-readable designation  
3. System applicability (3D frame, 2D plane/disk (“2D”), 2DSL plate/girder)  
4. Result file load-case numbers (max/min)  

Below is a breakdown of its structure and contents:

1. Header row  
   • “TYPE”: a short alphanumeric identifier used in the input commands (e.g. “PX”).  
   • “Designation”: full description of what that TYPE represents.  
   • “3D”, “2D”, “2DSL”: asterisks (*) indicate that the TYPE is available for superposition in that class of analysis (three-dimensional frame, two-dimensional plane/disk, or plate/girder).  
   • “Load case number S max/min”: the two integers separated by “/” are the record numbers in the MAXIMA result file at which the maximum and minimum superposition factors are stored.

2. Row groups  

   A. Support reactions  
     – PX: Support reaction in X direction  
       • Available in 3D and 2D.  
       • Load cases 51 / 52 for max/min.  
     – PY: Support reaction in Y direction  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 53 / 54.  
     – PZ: Support reaction in Z direction  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 55 / 56.  
     – P: All support reactions (PX, PY, PZ, MX, MY, MZ) in one group  
       • 3D, 2D and 2DSL.  
       • Cases  — stored at all three coordinates: 51/52, 53/54, 55/56 (implied).  

   B. Support moments  
     – MX: Support moment about X axis  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 57 / 58.  
     – MY: Support moment about Y axis  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 59 / 60.  
     – MZ: Support moment about Z axis  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 61 / 62.  
     – MB: Support warping moment (torsional warping)  
       • 3D only.  
       • Cases 91 / 92.  

   C. Nodal displacements  
     – UX: Nodal displacement in X direction  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 71 / 72.  
     – UY: Nodal displacement in Y direction  
       • 3D & 2D.  
       • Cases 73 / 74.  
     – UZ: Nodal displacement in Z direction  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 75 / 76.  

   D. Nodal rotations  
     – URX: Nodal rotation about X axis  
       • 3D & 2DSL.  
       • Cases 77 / 78.  
     – URY: Nodal rotation about Y axis  
       • 3D & 2D.  
       • Cases 79 / 80.  
     – (URZ would follow similarly in a complete table.)  

3. Usage context  

   In order to request all of these scalar variables for superposition in one go, the user can invoke:  
     SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO  
   which picks every available element type and its corresponding scalar variables. For finer control—say only beam-type data—the input would be:  
     SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO STAB TYPE AUTO  
   then refine the printout by specifying FROM/TO/INC to list only certain element numbers or groups.  

4. Notes  

   • The asterisks under the system columns ensure that you only request types that make sense for your model geometry (e.g. you won’t get a Z-displacement in a pure 2D planar analysis unless 2DSL is used).  
   • If you only superimpose displacements or rotations (without reactions), MAXIMA still prints zeroed support-reaction factors in its ECHO FACT list for completeness.  
   • When using ETYP SPAC (space elements), you must combine it with COMB EXTR NONL or STAN.  

This table is an indispensable cross-reference for scripting post-processing extracts in MAXIMA, making sure you pull exactly the superposition factors you need, for the right system type, stored at the correct load-case indices.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table shown is an excerpt from the MAXIMA input specification under “for nodes – ETYP NODE.”  It defines two scalar variables (nodal rotations) that may be superimposed and specifies in which kinds of static systems they are available, plus the load-case codes assigned to their extreme (max/min) factors in the output.  Below is a field-by-field breakdown:

1. Column 1 – TYPE  
   • URZ  
     – Code name for the nodal rotation about the global Z-axis  
   • URB  
     – Code name for the nodal rotation due to the warping moment  

2. Column 2 – Designation  
   • URZ: “Nodal rotation about Z direction”  
   • URB: “Nodal rotation due to warping moment”  

3. Column 3 – 3D  
   Marks whether the variable is available when the system is modeled as a full three-dimensional structure.  
   • URZ: “*” (available)  
   • URB: “*” (available)  

4. Column 4 – 2D  
   Marks availability in a planar frame or disk (“plane frame/disk”) analysis.  
   • URZ: “*” (available)  
   • URB: blank (not available)  

5. Column 5 – 2DSL  
   Marks availability in a plate or girder (“plate/girder”) analysis.  
   • URZ: blank (not available)  
   • URB: blank (not available)  

6. Column 6 – Load case number (max/min)  
   Gives the two factor-output case numbers that MAXIMA will assign to the positive and negative extremes of this variable in the support-reaction factor list (the factors always appear there, even if they are zero or the variable itself was not superimposed).  
   • URZ → 81/82 (81 for the maximum‐factor entry, 82 for the minimum‐factor entry)  
   • URB → 83/84 (83 for the max, 84 for the min)  

Contextual notes:  
– This table is used when ETYP NODE is active, meaning you have requested superposition of nodal displacements/rotations.  
– If only nodal displacements/rotations are superimposed, MAXIMA does not print factors in the displacement list (ECHO FACT) but always prints them in the support reactions list.  
– SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO (or, if you restrict to certain element types, e.g. beams: SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO STAB TYPE AUTO FROM … TO … INC) controls which element-type blocks (and thus which scalar variables) are included in the superposition.  
– The three system-type columns (3D, 2D, 2DSL) correspond to the static‐system settings in column 3 of the main input (i.e. 3D = full 3D; 2D = plane frame/disk; 2DSL = plate/girder).  

In practice, if you request SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP NODE AUTO, both URZ and URB will be included for 3D runs; URZ alone for 2D runs.  The load-case codes 81/82 and 83/84 will then appear in the factor printout alongside other support-reaction cases.

content:
The fragment shown is a portion of the “superposition variables” table for nodal dynamic quantities (velocities and accelerations) in a structural-analysis context. It defines six two-letter TYPE codes, each tied to one scalar nodal quantity, and maps them to the system dimensionality in which they may be superimposed, as well as the load-case numbers assigned to their maximum and minimum values when output. Below is a detailed breakdown of its structure and meaning:

1. Columns and Headings  
   • TYPE – a two-letter identifier for each scalar quantity:  
     – VX, VY, VZ: nodal velocities in X, Y, Z directions  
     – AX, AY, AZ: nodal accelerations in X, Y, Z directions  
   • Designation – a concise description of the physical meaning of each TYPE code.  
   • 3D – a star (*) indicates that the quantity is available for superposition in a full three-dimensional system.  
   • 2D – a star (*) indicates availability in a plane frame or disk model.  
   • 2DSL – a star (*) denotes availability in a plate or girder (shell/plate) model.  
   • Load case number max/min – two integers separated by “/” specify the load-case indices used to collect the maximum and minimum values of that quantity for reporting in the ECHO FACT list.

2. Row-by-Row Content  
   • VX: “Nodal velocity in X direction”  
     – Available in 3D and 2D analyses (stars under 3D and 2D); not applicable to 2DSL.  
     – Uses load cases 51 (max) and 52 (min).  
   • VY: “Nodal velocity in Y direction”  
     – Available in 3D and 2D; not in 2DSL.  
     – Load cases 53 (max) and 54 (min).  
   • VZ: “Nodal velocity in Z direction”  
     – Available in 3D and 2DSL; not in 2D.  
     – Load cases 55 (max) and 56 (min).  
   • AX: “Nodal acceleration in X direction”  
     – Available in 3D and 2D; not in 2DSL.  
     – Load cases 57 (max) and 58 (min).  
   • AY: “Nodal acceleration in Y direction”  
     – Available in 3D and 2D; omitted in 2DSL.  
     – Load cases 59 (max) and 60 (min).  
   • AZ: “Nodal acceleration in Z direction”  
     – Available in 3D and 2DSL; not in 2D.  
     – Load cases 61 (max) and 62 (min).

3. Context of Use  
   • Superposition Input: These nodal quantities are invoked via the ETYP NODE or ETYP SPAC keywords in a SUPP (support-reaction) superposition command.  
   • System Selection: If ETYP AUTO is used, all element and node types are automatically included. To restrict superposition to specific element types or nodes, one would append “STAB TYPE AUTO” or “FROM … TO … INC …” options.  
   • Output: MAXIMA computes and prints superposition factors for these nodal displacements or rotations in the support-reaction listing, even if a particular quantity is not active (in which case its factor appears as zero). If only nodal displacements/rotations are superposed without support reactions, no factors appear in the nodal-displacement ECHO FACT; instead they remain tied to support-reaction ECHO FACT.

4. Relation to Other Element Types  
   While this snippet focuses on nodal velocities and accelerations, the extended documentation also enumerates other ETYP codes—BEAM, DSLN, BSCT, TRUS, CABL, SPRI, CFM, QUAD, QNOD, QBED, BRIC, BNOD, SLVL—each with its own scalar variables, availability flags, and load-case numbering conventions.

By understanding the mapping shown in this table, users can precisely control which nodal kinematic quantities are included in a given superposition run and know exactly which load-case indices the software will employ to extract extreme values for post-processing reports.

content:
The excerpted table is part of the MAXIMA/TALPA input‐/output specification for support‐reaction superposition in different structural element types and static systems. It defines the internal “TYPE” codes, their textual designations, the system‐dimensional applicability flags, and the load‐case numbering conventions. Below is a breakdown of its structure and contents:

1. Table Layout  
   • Column 1 “TYPE”  
     – A two‐ or three-letter code identifying the result quantity.  
   • Column 2 “Designation”  
     – A brief English description of the variable.  
   • Columns 3–5 “3D”, “2D”, “2DSL”  
     – An asterisk (*) in each of these columns indicates that the variable is available for superposition in that system type:  
       • 3D: fully three-dimensional solid/space model  
       • 2D: plane frame or axisymmetric disk (plane stress/strain)  
       • 2DSL: plate, shell or girder (plate/girder elements)  
   • Column 6 “Load case number / S max/min / L”  
     – Specifies the numbering scheme for the load cases and whether the program will extract the maximum or minimum value (“S”) or simply list (“L”).  
   • Column 7 “Reference pages”  
     – The manual pages where this variable is described in detail (e.g. “63/64”).

2. Example Rows  
   – TYPE = PX  
     * Designation: “Support reaction in X direction of the boundary elements”  
     * Available in: 3D (*) and 2DSL (*), not in 2D (blank)  
     * Load-case numbering: pages 63/64  
   – TYPE = PY  
     * Designation: “Support reaction in Y direction of the boundary elements”  
     * Available in: 3D (*) and 2DSL (*)  
     * Load-case numbering: pages 65/66  
   – TYPE = PZ  
     * Designation: “Support reaction in Z direction of the boundary elements”  
     * Available in: 3D (*) and 2DSL (*)  
     * Load-case numbering: pages 67/68  

3. How This Table Fits Into Superposition Input  
   • SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO  
     – By default, all element types (nodes, beams, plates, volume elements, etc.) and their scalar result variables are included in the superposition.  
   • Targeted Selection  
     – To restrict the superposition variables to certain element types, you add “STAB TYPE AUTO” (e.g. for beams).  
     – You can then further prune the printout by specifying element or group ranges via “FROM … TO … INC ….”  
   • Special ETYP Keywords  
     – Beyond PX/PY/PZ for boundary‐element reactions, the manual lists ETYP codes for:  
       • NODE (displacements, rotations)  
       • SPAC (special combination with COMB EXTR NONL/STAN)  
       • BEAM, DSLN, BSCT (beam internal forces, section results)  
       • TRUS (truss‐bar forces)  
       • CABL (cable tension), SPRI (spring forces), CFM (kinematic constraints)  
       • QUAD/QNOD (plane elements stresses/forces), QBED (plane‐element bedding), BRIC/BNOD (brick/volume elements)  
       • SLVL (storey‐level seismic design results)  

4. Interpretation for a RAG Vector Store  
   • As you index this table, capture each row as a document with fields:  
     – type_code = “PX” / “PY” / “PZ”  
     – description = “Support reaction in X/Y/Z direction of the boundary elements”  
     – applicable_in_3d (bool), applicable_in_2d (bool), applicable_in_2dsl (bool)  
     – load_case_pages = “63/64” / “65/66” / “67/68”  
     – superposition_flag = “S max/min” or “L” (as indicated)  
   • Link the overall ETYP AUTO mechanism to the generic SUPP command usage (e.g. SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO).  

This detailed mapping will allow a retrieval‐augmented system to answer questions such as “Which ETYP codes are valid for plate elements?” or “What page do I consult for the Z-reaction superposition?”, and to guide users to the correct manual sections.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table shown is a concise reference for how the MAXIMA/TALPA system handles superposition of internal quantities on boundary‐type elements, when you request ETYP BOUN (single boundary elements) or ETYP BOUS (sums of boundary elements).  In the broader context of the static‐system input (3D frame, 2D plane frame/disk, or 2DSL plate/girder), each row in this table associates

  • a one‐letter TYPE code  
  • a human‐readable “Designation” of the quantity to be superimposed  
  • applicability flags for each system dimensionality (columns headed “3 D”, “2 D” and “2 D S”)  
  • an optional “Load case number max/min” field indicating which internal MAXIMA case IDs hold the extreme values

Because the system allows “ETYP AUTO” (all element types) or a specific ETYP (in this case BOUN/BOUS) together with SUPP/EXTR/MAMI, you pick out just boundary‐element variables and steer which ones the program will superpose.  If you instead do “ETYP AUTO”, you get every available scalar variable across beams, shells, solids, etc., possibly at the expense of longer run‐times in large heterogeneous models.

Detailed breakdown of the two rows in your snippet:

1) TYPE P  
   – Designation: “All support reaction of the boundary elements.”  
   – Applicability: a “*” in the 3 D, 2 D and 2 D S columns means you can request P in all three system types (3D frame, plane frame or plate/girder).  
   – Load case field: blank, which implies that the program does not assign a specific case number to track extremes—when you ask for P, you simply get whichever reaction values occur under the various load combinations or superposition definitions.

2) TYPE M  
   – Designation: “Moment about the edge.”  
   – Applicability: “*” under 3 D and under 2 D S, but no star under plain 2 D.  That tells you that edge moments are defined in 3D and plate/girder contexts, but not in a pure in‐plane disk/frame scenario.  
   – Load case number “69/70”: these two integers are the internal MAXIMA case IDs corresponding to the maximum and minimum moment values, respectively.  When the routine does its ultimate extreme search, it stores the index of the load case that produced the positive maximum in case 69 and the negative extremum in case 70.

How you actually invoke these:

• To superpose all boundary reactions (TYPE P) in an automatic pick of all element types, you might use  
     SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP BOUS  
  or for single‐element printing:  
     SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP BOUN

• If you only want moments about edges (TYPE M) you could still use ETYP BOUN, but the program will only report M for 3D and plate cases; it will suppress it (or print zero factors) if you happen to be in 2D.

• If you need to filter to a subset of boundary elements (e.g. elements 50–75 in steps of 1), append  
     FROM 50 TO 75 INC 1  
  after the ETYP keyword.

In sum, the table is a lookup that tells the pre‐ and post‐processor:

  – “Which internal scalar variables exist for boundary‐element superposition?”  
  – “In which system types are they valid?”  
  – “What internal result‐set indices track their global extremes?”

This pattern reappears for other ETYPs (BEAM, TRUS, CABL, QUAD, BRIC, etc.), each with its own TYPE codes (N, V, M, T, …), applicability flags, and load‐case indices for max/min.  Using these tables, you compose SUPP/EXTR statements that yield exactly the reaction, force, moment or stress envelopes you need, no more and no less.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
Below is a structured description of the extract from the input‐table, augmented by the surrounding context you supplied. This table defines which global support‐reaction and support‐moment quantities can be superimposed (ETYP BOUN/BOUS) and flagged for 3D, 2D (plane frame), or 2DSL (plate/girder) analyses in the MAXIMA system. An asterisk “*” marks availability; the right‐hand column lists the load‐case references where maxima and minima are printed.

1. Table Columns  
   • TYPE  
     – A short code identifying the quantity.  
   • Designation  
     – A natural‐language description of the summed reaction or moment.  
   • 3D D  
     – Applicable in three‐dimensional analyses. D stands for displacement superposition.  
   • 2D D  
     – Applicable in plane‐frame/plane‐disk analyses.  
   • 2DSL S L  
     – Applicable to plate/girder (“2DSL”) analyses. S and L indicate stress or load superposition.  
   • Load-case number max/min  
     – The two page references in the MAXIMA output (first for max, second for min) where the printed values can be found.

2. Table Rows and Entries  
   PX  
     • Sum support reaction in the global X-direction of all boundary elements.  
     • Available for 3D and 2D frames (asterisks under both “3D D” and “2D D”).  
     • On pages 83 and 84 of the ECHO FACT report.  
   PY  
     • Sum support reaction in the global Y-direction of boundary elements.  
     • Available for 3D and 2D.  
     • Printed in load cases on pages 85 (max) and 86 (min).  
   PZ  
     • Sum support reaction in the global Z-direction.  
     • Available in 3D only (asterisk under “3D D”).  
     • Pages 87 and 88.  
   P  
     • Total sum of all support reactions (|PX|+|PY|+|PZ|).  
     • Available in all three system types (3D, 2D, and 2DSL).  
     • Load-case printout on pages 83/84 for 3D, 85/86 for 2D, 87/88 for 2DSL.  
   M  
     • Sum of support moments about a specified edge (the global moment resultant).  
     • Available in 3D and 2DSL (asterisks under “3D D” and “2DSL L”).  
     • Printed on pages 89 (max) and 90 (min).

3. Notes on Usage and Superposition Factors  
   – This table is part of the ETYP BOUN (boundary elements) and ETYP BOUS (sum of boundary elements) superposition framework.  
   – The program MAXIMA computes factors for nodal displacements/rotations or support reactions/moments and prints them alongside the standard ECHO FACT output. If you request only nodal quantities, MAXIMA still lists zero‐values of support factors in the reaction table.  
   – The asterisks indicate that you can invoke summation of that quantity under the respective analysis type by including ETYP AUTO or explicitly listing ETYP BOUN/BOUS with FROM–TO–INC if you want a subset of elements/groups.  
   – When using “ETYP SPAC”, the same table format applies, but only in combination with COMB EXTR NONL or STAN.  

In practice, to generate the sums for boundary‐element reactions in all supported coordinate directions and total reaction, you would use an input line such as:  
   SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO  
and the output will include PX, PY, PZ, P, and M (plus any other ETYP BOUN entries) marked with their respective asterisks and page references for max/min results.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table shown is the definition of all scalar internal‐force and moment quantities that the system will superimpose and report for beam-type elements (ETYP BEAM, DSLN, BSCT) when you request ETYP AUTO (or explicitly ETYP BEAM with STAB TYPE AUTO).  Each row corresponds to one “TYPE” code (the short name you would use in your input), and each column tells you:

 1. TYPE  
    – The two- or three-letter code you refer to in the input (e.g. “N”, “VY”, “MY” etc.).  
 2. Designation  
    – A brief English description of what that code stands for.  
 3. 3D D  
    – A “*” in this column means the quantity is available for superposition in a three-dimensional space‐frame (three translational DOFs per node).  
 4. 2D D  
    – A “*” here means it is available in a 2D plane‐frame or disk model (two translational DOFs per node).  
 5. 2DSL  
    – A “*” here means it is available in a 2D plate/girder model (three DOFs per node: two translations + rotation).  
 6. Load case number max/min  
    – Two integers separated by “/” that tell you under which envelope‐case numbers the maximum and minimum values will be printed in the ECHO FACT list.  

Below is a line-by-line description:

 • N  
   – Beam normal (axial) force  
   – Available in 3D D, 2D D and 2DSL (asterisks in all three columns)  
   – Printed as envelope cases 21 (max) / 22 (min)  

 • VY  
   – Shear force in the local Y-direction  
   – Available only in 3D D  
   – Printed as cases 23 / 24  

 • VZ  
   – Shear force in the local Z-direction  
   – Available in 3D D and 2DSL  
   – Printed as cases 25 / 26  

 • MT  
   – Torsional (twisting) moment about the beam’s longitudinal axis  
   – Available in 3D D and 2DSL  
   – Printed as cases 27 / 28  

 • MY  
   – Bending moment about the local Y-axis  
   – Available in 3D D, 2D D and 2DSL  
   – Printed as cases 29 / 30  

 • MZ  
   – Bending moment about the local Z-axis  
   – Available in 3D D and 2DSL  
   – Printed as cases 31 / 32  

 • MB  
   – Warping moment (only in 3D–torsion with open sections)  
   – Available only in 3D D  
   – Printed as cases 33 / 34  

 • MT2  
   – Secondary torsional moment (Saint-Venant)  
   – Available only in 3D D  
   – Printed as cases 35 / 36  

How this ties into the overall workflow:  
– When you enter “SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO” (or “SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP BEAM STAB TYPE AUTO”), the program MAXIMA computes superposition factors for all supported scalar variables of the chosen element types (here, beams).  
– If you only superimpose nodal displacements or rotations (ETYP NODE), you will not see any factors in the displacement list (ECHO FACT), but you will still get zero‐valued factors printed in the support‐reaction list.  
– You may further restrict the output to a subset of elements or to particular variable codes by using a FROM–TO–INC range specification.  

In sum, this table documents exactly which internal forces and moments are collected, in which modeling context (3D, plane, plate), and under which envelope case numbers the maxima and minima are reported when you request automatic superposition of beam results.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table is part of the MAXIMA/TALPA input schema for defining which scalar result-quantities are to be superimposed and printed in a static or dynamic analysis. It identifies each variable by a short code (“TYPE”), gives a human-readable “Designation,” indicates in which dimensional system(s) it applies, and shows the corresponding load-case numbers for maximum and minimum superposition results. In practice you invoke these with commands such as   
    SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO  
or, for a restricted set of element types,  
    SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO STAB TYPE AUTO  
possibly followed by FROM/TO/INC to select subsets of elements or groups.

1. Column Layout  
 • TYPE  
   – A short mnemonic.  
 • Designation  
   – A textual description of the quantity.  
 • Applicability Flags (three subcolumns labelled “3 D,” “2 D,” “2 DSL”)  
   – An asterisk (*) means the quantity is available for that system:  
     • 3 D = three-dimensional frame or solid  
     • 2 D = plane frame or disk  
     • 2 DSL = plate/girder element  
 • Load-case number max/min  
   – Two integers separated by “/” give the automatically assigned load-case IDs under which the maximum and minimum superposition results will be stored and printed.  

2. Node-based Variables (ETYP NODE)  
 UX  
   – Displacement u-x; available in 3 D and 2 DSL; load cases 71/72  
 UY  
   – Displacement u-y; available in 2 D and 2 DSL; load cases 73/74  
 UZ  
   – Displacement u-z; available in all three systems; load cases 75/76  
 URX  
   – Rotation ϕ-x; available in 3 D and 2 DSL; load cases 77/78  
 URY  
   – Rotation ϕ-y; available in 3 D and 2 DSL; load cases 79/80  
 URZ  
   – Rotation ϕ-z; available in 3 D and 2 DSL; load cases 81/82  
 URB  
   – Warping rotation; available only in 2 DSL; load cases 93/94  

3. Beam and Design-Element Section Stresses (in combination with SELE for BEAM or DSLN)  
 SIG  
   – Normal stress at a cross-section point; available in all three systems; load cases 11/12  
 TAU  
   – Shear stress at a cross-section point; available in all three systems; load cases 15/16  
   • Note: When the superposition type is “STRESS,” MAXIMA actually computes internal forces/moments and leaves final stress combination to a plane-strain run in TALPA.

4. Pile-Bedding Reactions (BEAM only)  
 PA  
   – Bedding in principal direction; available in 3 D and 2 DSL; load cases 37/38  
 PTY  
   – Transverse bedding in y; available in 3 D and 2 DSL; load cases 95/96  
 PTZ  
   – Transverse bedding in z; available in 3 D and 2 DSL; load cases 97/98  

Key Remarks:  
- If only nodal displacements or rotations are superimposed, no factors appear in the ECHO FACT list, but zero-value factors are still printed under support reactions.  
- ETYP SPAC can only be combined with COMB EXTR NONL or STAN.  
- Other element classes (truss bars, cables, springs, boundary elements, volume elements, seismic storey results, etc.) each have analogous TYPE codes, defined elsewhere in the manual.

content:
The fragment you have provided is the “cable” entry out of a larger table that defines, for each structural element type, which scalar result quantities can be superposed (ETYP AUTO) and where they will appear in the printed output.  Below is a detailed, column-by-column description of the cable line:

1. Overall context  
   • This is part of the ETYP CABL section (i.e. “for cables”).  
   • The table’s purpose is to tell MAXIMA which internal forces or results (scalar variables) are available for superposition, and in which structural‐analysis settings (3D, 2D, or 2DSL) they apply.  
   • The far‐right column gives the output positions––the “load case numbers”––where the maximum and minimum values of each variable will be printed.

2. Column headings  
   • TYPE  
     – A short code identifying the scalar quantity (here “N”).  
   • Designation  
     – A text description of the quantity (“Normal force of the cable”).  
   • 3D D  
     – A flag (*) indicating that this quantity is defined for three-dimensional analyses (space frames).  
   • 2D D  
     – A flag (*) indicating that this quantity is defined for two-dimensional frame or disk analyses.  
   • 2DSL L  
     – A flag indicating plate/girder (2DSL) applicability.  (Empty here, so normal‐force superposition is not available in 2DSL plate/girder models.)  
   • Load case number Smax/min L  
     – The two positions in the printed load‐case listing where the maximum (first number) and minimum (second number) of this quantity will appear.  

3. The single data row (for cables)  
   TYPE:  
     – N  
   Designation:  
     – Normal force of the cable  
   3D D:  
     – *  (Available in 3D superposition.)  
   2D D:  
     – *  (Available in 2D superposition.)  
   2DSL L:  
     – (blank)  – Not available for plate/girder superposition.  
   Load case number Smax/min L:  
     – 43 / 44  
       • “43” is the column or block number under which MAXIMA will print the maximum cable‐force result when you request superposition of internal forces.  
       • “44” is the analogous position for the minimum cable‐force result.

4. How it fits into the workflow  
   • If you request “SUPP … ETYP AUTO,” then for element type CABL, MAXIMA will include the cable’s normal force “N” in the superposition calculation for both 3D and 2D systems, and show the extremes in positions 43/44 of the load‐case printout.  
   • If you instead do “SUPP … ETYP CABL,” you could limit the superposition only to cables, still picking up N.  
   • Flags in the 3D/2D/2DSL columns ensure you do not accidentally try to superpose cable normal forces in plate/girder contexts where they are undefined.

In summary, this table row tells you that “N – Normal force of the cable” is a valid superposition variable in both space‐frame (3D) and planar‐frame (2D) analyses, and that its maximum and minimum values will be printed in load‐case columns 43 and 44, respectively.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table excerpt shown is part of the MAXIMA/TALPA user-manual’s description of “ETYP AUTO” superposition output for spring (SUPRI) elements. It defines which scalar results can be extracted when you request a superposition of spring forces, displacements or rotations, and it tells you the corresponding load‐case index numbers for the max/min values. Below is a breakdown of its structure and content:

1. Overall Structure  
   • Five columns, with these headings (left to right):  
     1. TYPE – the short code used in input or output lists.  
     2. Designation – the full textual description of the variable.  
     3. 3D D – marked with “*” if the variable is available in three-dimensional analyses.  
     4. 2D D – marked with “*” if the variable is available in two-dimensional (plane frame or disk) analyses.  
     5. 2DSL S L – marked with “*” if the variable is available in plate/girder (2DSL) analyses.  
   • A final legend at the right gives the Load Case numbers for the maximum and minimum of each variable (e.g. “45/46” means 45 for max, 46 for min).

2. Column‐by‐Column Explanation  
   a. TYPE  
      – Unique identifier used when you specify ETYP SPRI.  
      – These abbreviations appear in both input commands and in the printed superposition results.  
   b. Designation  
      – Plain-language name of the scalar quantity.  
      – Makes clear whether it is a force, moment, displacement or rotation, and along which axis.  
   c. 3D D, 2D D, 2DSL S L  
      – A “*” in a column means that MAXIMA can compute and superpose that variable in that class of model.  
      – If a column is blank, that variable is not meaningful (or not implemented) for that system type.  
   d. Load case number max/min  
      – Two integers separated by “/.”  
      – The first is the load‐case index where the maximum value occurs, the second where the minimum occurs.  
      – Used internally if you ask for “ECHO FACT” or when MAMI (moment output) is requested.

3. Row-by-Row Contents  
   • P  
     – “Spring force in main direction” (axial spring force)  
     – Available in 3D, 2D, 2DSL (***).  
     – Load case numbers: 45 (max) / 46 (min).  
   • PTX, PTY, PTZ  
     – “Spring transverse force” in X, Y, Z respectively.  
     – PTX: available in 3D & 2DSL (* *  ), cases 93/94.  
     – PTY: available in 3D & 2DSL (* *  ), cases 95/96.  
     – PTZ: available in 3D & 2DSL (* *  ), cases 97/98.  
   • M  
     – “Spring moment” (about the spring’s local axis)  
     – Available in all systems (***).  
     – Cases 47/48.  
   • U  
     – “Spring displacement in main direction” (axial deflection)  
     – All systems (***).  
     – Cases 49/50.  
   • UTX, UTY, UTZ  
     – “Spring transverse displacement” in X, Y, Z.  
     – UTX & UTY: available in 3D & 2DSL (* *  ), cases 73/74 & 75/76.  
     – UTZ: available in 3D & 2DSL (* *  ), cases 77/78.  
   • UR  
     – “Spring rotation about main direction” (torsional rotation)  
     – All systems (***).  
     – Cases 51/52.  

4. How to Use This Table in a RAG/Vector‐Store Workflow  
   – If you issue  
     SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP SPRI  
     MAXIMA will superimpose/support‐reactions for all spring elements and print out only those variables marked “*” under the chosen system dimension.  
   – If you only want, say, transverse spring displacements in X (UTX) for a subset of elements or load cases, you would combine ETYP SPRI with FROM/TO/INC filters and the TYPE code “UTX.”  
   – The load‐case columns let you trace back which input load case produced the extreme value for each variable.  

By organizing variable availability and load‐case indices in this way, the table provides a concise reference for automating post-processing scripts (e.g. in a RAG pipeline). You can map each TYPE code to its human‐readable name and dimension applicability, then link it to the corresponding load‐case number when you ingest superposition results into your vector store.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table shown is an excerpt from the MAXIMA/TALPA user documentation that defines how “coupling” forces and moments at a node are handled when you request a superposition (ETYP SPAC) of support reactions. It has five columns and six data rows. Below is a detailed, column‐by‐column and row‐by‐row breakdown, together with the contextual meaning of the asterisks and load‐case numbers:

1. Column 1 – “TYPE”  
   This is the short code you feed into the ETYP SPAC command to specify which coupling component you want to superimpose. The valid codes here are:  
   • PX  
   • PY  
   • PZ  
   • P  (all coupling forces at once)  
   • MX  
   • MY  

2. Column 2 – “Designation”  
   A textual description of what each TYPE code stands for:  
   • PX – “Coupling force in X direction”  
   • PY – “Coupling force in Y direction”  
   • PZ – “Coupling force in Z direction”  
   • P  – “All coupling forces” (i.e. X, Y, Z together)  
   • MX – “Coupling moment about the X direction”  
   • MY – “Coupling moment about the Y direction”  

3. Columns 3–5 – Static‐system applicability  
   These three columns each correspond to one of the three “static system” settings you can select when preparing a superposition:  
   • Column 3 (“3D D”) applies if the model is a fully three‐dimensional frame or solid.  
   • Column 4 (“2D D”) applies if the model is a planar frame or disk (plane‐frame/disk).  
   • Column 5 (“2DSL SL” – plate/girder) applies if the model is a plate or girder (2D shell‐like elements).  
   An asterisk “*” in any of these columns means that the given coupling force or moment can be extracted as part of the superposition for that system type. A blank means it is not available for that system.  
   • PX, PY, PZ each show “*” in the appropriate axes columns (e.g. PX has “*” under 3D and 2D, but blank under 2DSL if the Z‐coupling is not defined for plates).  
   • P (all forces) shows “*” under all three system types, since you can request the full vector of coupling forces in any dimension.  
   • MX, MY typically appear under 3D and 2D only, because moments about X or Y are not defined for pure plate/girder theory unless you treat them as shell elements with bending moments.  

4. Column 6 – “Load case number max/min”  
   Once you ask MAXIMA to superimpose these coupling components, it assigns two internal “load‐case numbers” where it stores the maximum and the minimum envelope values. These numbers are shown as “positive/negative” case indices:  
   • PX → 51/52  
   • PY → 53/54  
   • PZ → 55/56  
   • P  → (not shown in the fragment but would typically follow)  
   • MX → 57/58  
   • MY → 59/60  

How this fits into the broader workflow:  
– All element types can be selected with ETYP AUTO to generate superpositions of every scalar result available. Subsets (e.g. only beams) can be picked with ETYP AUTO combined with STAB TYPE and further refined by FROM/TO/INC.  
– ETYP SPAC is reserved for nodal coupling‐force superposition and only works when you have called COMB EXTR NONL or STAN.  
– Even if you do a pure displacement/rotation superposition, the coupling‐force factors still appear in the support‐reaction list (echoed with ECHO FACT). The load‐case slots listed above are where MAXIMA writes the envelope results for each coupling component.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The excerpted table is part of the MAXIMA/TALPA static‐system input reference.  It defines two “coupling moment” scalar quantities (MZ and MB), shows for which system geometries they can be requested, and assigns each a pair of load‐case identifiers for the superposition of its maximum and minimum values.  

1. Table layout  
   • Columns (left to right):  
     1. TYPE  
        – A short code used in the ETYP… input to select that quantity for superposition.  
     2. Designation  
        – A brief English description of what the code represents.  
     3. 3 D (three‐dimensional system)  
        – An asterisk (*) indicates that MAXIMA will compute and superimpose this scalar in a full 3D solid/beam model.  
     4. 2 D (plane‐frame or disk)  
        – An asterisk means it is available when the model has only two‐dimensional frame or disk elements.  
     5. 2 DSL (plate or girder)  
        – An asterisk here would mark availability for plate or girder (2 D shell‐like) analyses; a blank means the quantity is not defined for that case.  
     6. Load‐case number – max  
     7. Load‐case number – min  
        – Together these two columns give the integer identifiers that MAXIMA assigns to the “maximum” (first number) and “minimum” (second number) results of the superposition run for that quantity.  

2. Row entries  
   • MZ  
     – TYPE code: MZ  
     – Designation: “Coupling moment about the Z direction.”  This is the moment that enforces compatibility between adjoining elements or substructures in the Z‐axis rotation.  
     – Applicability:  
        • 3 D → *  (available)  
        • 2 D → *  (available)  
        • 2 DSL →   (not available)  
     – Load‐case IDs: 61 (maximum), 62 (minimum)  
   • MB  
     – TYPE code: MB  
     – Designation: “Coupling warping moment.”  Represents the torsional‐warping compatibility moment in 3D beam or solid elements.  
     – Applicability:  
        • 3 D → *  (available)  
        • 2 D →   (not available)  
        • 2 DSL →   (not available)  
     – Load‐case IDs: 91 (maximum), 92 (minimum)  

3. Usage notes  
   – To request superposition of these coupling moments, include their TYPE codes in an ETYP … input (e.g. ETYP BEAM, ETYP AUTO, or a manually specified list).  
   – MAXIMA will then compute nodal reactions or element forces, extract the relevant coupling moment, and assign the results to the specified load‐case numbers.  When you later apply the COMB EXTR command (or similar), you can refer to load‐cases 61/62 (for MZ) or 91/92 (for MB) to gather maxima and minima into envelope results.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table is a reference for all of the scalar result‐types that can be superimposed when you use ETYP AUTO (or when you explicitly pick one of the element types).  It shows, for each result TYPE code,  
 1. A short text designation  
 2. Which system‐dimensions it applies to (3D solid, 2D frame/disk or 2D shell/plate)  
 3. The “load‐case number” pair (max/min) under which MAXIMA stores the superposition factors  

Column headings  
• TYPE – the mnemonic code you enter (or that appears in the output)  
• Designation – a brief description of what the scalar is  
• 3D – a star (*) if this result makes sense in a three-dimensional solid element  
• 2D – a star if it applies in a planar frame or disk element  
• 2DSL – a star if it applies in a plate, shell or girder (“2D shell”) element  
• Load case number max/min – the two‐digit codes under which MAXIMA prints the positive/negative‐extreme superposition factors  

1. Bending moments (beams and frame members)  
   • MXX – “Bending moment m-xx”  
       3D *, 2D * → LC 01/02  
   • MYY – “Bending moment m-yy”  
       3D *, 2D * → LC 03/04  
   • MXY – “Torsional moment m-xy”  
       3D *, 2D * → LC 05/06  
   • M – “All bending moments” (superposition of MXX, MYY, MXY)  
       3D *, 2D * → no load‐case pair (it is a combined result)  

2. Shear forces (beams and frames)  
   • VX – “Shear force v-x”  
       3D *, 2D * → LC 07/08  
   • VY – “Shear force v-y”  
       3D *, 2D * → LC 09/10  

3. In‐plane stresses for disk elements (ETYP DSLN or external sections ETYP BSCT when used as disk)  
   • SX – “Stress in x-direction”  
       2DSL * → LC 11/12  
   • SY – “Stress in y-direction”  
       2DSL * → LC 13/14  
   • SXY – “Shear stress in plane”  
       2DSL * → LC 15/16  
   • SZ – “Stress normal to disk plane”  
       2DSL * → LC 17/18  
   • S – “Combined stress” (SX + SY + SXY)  
       2DSL * → no separate load‐case pair (it is a summary result)  

4. Membrane internal forces for shell elements (ETYP QUAD/BRIC/BNOD interpreted as shells)  
   • NXX – “Membrane internal force N-xx”  
       3D *, 2DSL * → LC 11/12  
   • NYY – “Membrane internal force N-yy”  
       3D *, 2DSL * → LC 13/14  
   • NXY – “Membrane shear force N-xy”  
       3D *, 2DSL * → LC 15/16  
   • N – “All membrane internal forces”  
       3D *, 2DSL * → no separate pair  

5. Shell bending stresses (plate/shell elements ETYP QUAD only)  
   – Upper side stresses  
     • SXT – σₓ-top (Shell stress at upper surface)  
         3D *, 2DSL * → LC 71/72  
     • SYT – σᵧ-top  
         3D *, 2DSL * → LC 73/74  
     • SXYT – τₓᵧ-top  
         3D *, 2DSL * → LC 75/76  
   – Lower side stresses  
     • SXB – σₓ-bottom  
         3D *, 2DSL * → LC 77/78  
     • SYB – σᵧ-bottom  
         3D *, 2DSL * → LC 79/80  
     • SXYB – τₓᵧ-bottom  
         3D *, 2DSL * → LC 81/82  
   • S – “Combined shell stress” (sum of all six above)  
       3D *, 2DSL * → no separate pair  

6. Prestress increment  
   • SIGT – “Stress increment (prestress)”  
       only for ETYP QUAD  

Notes:  
- An asterisk in the 3D/2D/2DSL columns means that MAXIMA includes that scalar when you superimpose results in that kind of element.  
- The load‐case number pairs are the identifiers under which MAXIMA writes the positive and negative extremal superposition factors into the support‐reaction list (even if that specific result is not directly a support reaction).  
- “M”, “N” and “S” rows represent combined summaries (no own load‐case codes).  
- If you choose ETYP AUTO, all of the above scalars available in the model will be superposed; if you instead restrict to, say, beams only (ETYP BEAM), you will get only the relevant subset (MXX, MYY, MXY, M, VX, VY).

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The fragment shown is part of the ETYP-AUTO superposition table for bedding (foundation) stresses in QUAD (four-node plane) elements.  In the context of a SUPP…EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO (or SUPP…ETYP AUTO STAB TYPE AUTO) run, it tells you which “P-type” bedding stresses you can request, in which kinds of finite-element systems, and where in the printed output you’ll find them.

1.  Column breakdown  
   •  TYPE  
      – The internal code you must supply after ETYP (here: P, PTX, PTY, PTZ).  
   •  Designation  
      – A short English description of each scalar result.  
   •  3D / 2D / 2DSL  
      – A star “*” in each of these three columns flags availability in that system type:  
         • 3D = three-dimensional solid models (BRIC, BNOD, etc.)  
         • 2D = plane-frame or axisymmetric “disk” models  
         • 2DSL = plate/girder or shell models  
   •  Load-case # / max-min  
      – Indicates that all load-cases are considered, the program selects maxima or minima among them, and it also shows the page references in the manual where the printed results appear (for example, “17/18” means pp. 17–18).

2.  Rows in the table  
   •  P  
      – Bedding stress in the main (normal) direction of a QUAD element.  
      – Available in 3D, 2D and 2DSL (all three columns have “*”).  
      – Printed under all load cases, extrema taken, see manual pp. 17–18.  
   •  PTX  
      – Tangential (shear) bedding component in the local X-direction of a QUAD.  
      – Available in 3D and 2D only (stars under those two columns).  
      – See printed output on pp. 93–94.  
   •  PTY  
      – Tangential bedding component in the local Y-direction.  
      – Available in 3D and 2DSL.  
      – Results printed on pp. 95–96.  
   •  PTZ  
      – Out-of-plane tangential bedding (Z-direction shear for QUAD).  
      – Only in full 3D systems.  
      – Listed in the printout on pp. 97–98.

3.  How to use it  
   – In your SUPP card you would write, for example:  
        SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO STAB TYPE AUTO  
     to superimpose all available scalar variables for all element types.  
   – If you only want to see the bedding stresses you can narrow it down:  
        SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP P,PTX,PTY,PTZ FROM … TO … INC …  
     or simply  
        SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP P,PTX,PTY,PTZ  
     noting that you must only request those codes defined for QUAD elements.  
   – The stars in the 3D/2D/2DSL columns remind you which system geometries support each result.

By referencing this mini-table when preparing your SUPP/ECHO cards, you ensure that MAXIMA will compute and print the correct bedding‐stress superposition factors for QUAD elements, in the system types you actually have in your model.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The table under discussion defines which stress‐type scalar outputs are available for “volume elements” (ETYP BRIC/BNOD) in a static superposition run (ETYP AUTO), and how they are numbered in the printed load‐case summaries. It also indicates in which kinds of systems (3D, 2D frame/disk, or 2DSL plate/girder) each stress quantity will be collected for superposition.  Below is a column‐by‐column and row‐by‐row breakdown:

1.  Column headings  
    •  “TYPE”  
       –  The short mnemonic used internally (and on printed tables) to denote each stress component.  
    •  “Designation”  
       –  A plain‐English description of the stress component in the global (x, y, z) coordinate system.  
    •  “3D”  
       –  A “*” indicates that this stress quantity is computed and superposed when the system is modeled as a full three‐dimensional continuum (volume elements).  
    •  “2D”  
       – If “*” appeared here, it would denote availability in a plane‐stress or plane‐strain 2D discretization. In this table none of the volume‐element stresses are relevant in 2D‐only models.  
    •  “2DSL”  
       – A “*” in this column would flag plate‐or‐girder (shell or layered plate) applicability. Again, none of the purely volumetric stress components superpose in that setting.  
    •  “Load case number S max/min L”  
       – For each stress type, the two integers separated by “/” give the record numbers under which the maximum (“max”) and minimum (“min”) superposition factors will appear in the printed support reaction lists (ECHO FACT). Even though these are nodal‐reaction listings, MAXIMA always tags in the stress superposition factors here, printing zero if not actually superposed.

2.  Row details  
    a.  SX  
        – Stress in global X‐direction  
        – Available in 3D (*)  
        – Max/min factor labels 11/12  
    b.  SY  
        – Stress in global Y‐direction  
        – Available in 3D (*)  
        – Max/min factor labels 13/14  
    c.  SXY  
        – Shear stress in the global XY plane  
        – Available in 3D (*)  
        – Max/min factor labels 15/16  
    d.  SZ  
        – Stress in global Z‐direction  
        – Available in 3D (*)  
        – Max/min factor labels 17/18  
    e.  SYZ  
        – Shear stress in the global YZ plane  
        – Available in 3D (*)  
        – Max/min factor labels 07/08  
    f.  SXZ  
        – Shear stress in the global XZ plane  
        – Available in 3D (*)  
        – Max/min factor labels 09/10  
    g.  S  
        – “All stresses in volume elements” (a unified view of the six independent stress components)  
        – Available in 3D (*)  
        – (No separate load‐case codes listed here; the program collates this under the same 3D superposition grouping.)

3.  How it fits into the superposition workflow  
    •  When you request ETYP AUTO (or explicitly ETYP BRIC/BNOD), MAXIMA cycles through every defined volume element and computes these stress quantities for each load case.  
    •  It then evaluates the superposition factors (combining load cases per COMB EXTR, etc.) but, by design, prints those factors only in the support‐reaction summary (ECHO FACT), tagging them by the number shown in the rightmost column.  
    •  If you restrict to plane‐element stresses (ETYP QUAD) or beam forces (ETYP BEAM), a similar table exists with its own codes; this one is solely for solid‐element stress outputs.  

In practice, to get them all at once for a 3D system you simply input:
   SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP AUTO
and MAXIMA will generate superposition factors and print the results for SX, SY, SXY, SZ, SYZ, SXZ and the aggregated S under the respective case numbers.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
Below is a structured, detailed description of the table you provided, which defines the “storey‐level” result types for seismic design superpositions (ETYP SLVL). The description spells out each column’s purpose, explains the row entries, and highlights how to invoke these items in the input deck.

1. Overall Context  
   – This table appears under the ETYP SLVL option, which governs superposition of seismic storey results.  
   – Each row defines one TYPE code (a two‐letter keyword) that you can request for output.  
   – An asterisk (“*”) in the 3D, 2D or 2DSL columns marks availability in that kind of model (three‐dimensional solid, plane frame/disk, or plate/girder).  
   – The final column gives the “Load case number” identifiers you must use to pick up the maximum or minimum value of that result in your printout.

2. Column‐by‐Column Breakdown  
   1) TYPE  
      • A two‐letter code you supply after ETYP SLVL to select which storey‐level quantity you want.  
   2) Designation  
      • A human‐readable description of what the code stands for.  
   3) 3D  
      • An asterisk means this result is computed and printed in a full 3D model.  
   4) 2D  
      • An asterisk means this result is valid in a 2D plane‐frame or disk model.  
   5) 2DSL  
      • An asterisk means the result is valid in a plate/girder (2DSL) model.  
   6) Load case number max/min  
      • Two integers separated by “/.”  
      • The first is the load‐case code for the maximum envelope value; the second is for the minimum.

3. Row‐by‐Row Descriptions

  • PX  
    – Base shear in the global X-direction at each storey level.  
    – Available in 3D, 2D and 2DSL (all marked “*”).  
    – Use load case codes 51 (max) and 52 (min).  

  • PY  
    – Base shear in the global Y-direction at each storey level.  
    – Available in 3D, 2D and 2DSL.  
    – Use load case codes 53 (max) and 54 (min).  

  • PZ  
    – Total vertical force at and above the storey in the global Z-direction.  
    – Available in 3D, 2D and 2DSL.  
    – Use load case codes 55 (max) and 56 (min).  

  • MX  
    – Overturning moment about the global X-axis for the storey.  
    – Available in all system types (3D, 2D, 2DSL).  
    – Use load case codes 59 (max) and 60 (min).  

  • MY  
    – Overturning moment about the global Y-axis for the storey.  
    – Available in 3D, 2D and 2DSL.  
    – Use load case codes 61 (max) and 62 (min).  

  • MZ  
    – Overturning moment about the global Z-axis for the storey.  
    – Available in 3D, 2D and 2DSL.  
    – Use load case codes 63 (max) and 64 (min).  

4. How to Invoke in an Input Deck  
   – To request all six storey‐level quantities in your superposition, you could use, for example:  
     SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP SLVL PX PY PZ MX MY MZ  
   – If you only want, say, the overturning moment about Y, you might write:  
     SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP SLVL MY  

5. Notes  
   – The load‐case numbers (e.g., 53/54 for PY) appear in the output listings of superposition factors.  
   – Even if a particular result isn’t superimposed, the program still prints its factor (zero) in the support‐reaction list.  
   – Always combine ETYP SLVL with proper COMB or EXTR options if performing nonlinear or standard superpositions.

This description should give you all you need to index, parse, or construct queries against these storey‐level seismic results in a RAG‐style vector database.

sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

content:
The excerpted table defines the story‐level output quantities (TYPE) that can be requested when doing a seismic “superposition” of results in the program (ETYP SLVL).  Each row corresponds to one of the seven available response measures, lists a short mnemonic (TYPE), gives an English description, indicates in which system types it is supported, and finally shows the two load‐case codes assigned to its maximum and minimum values.  Here is a breakdown of its structure and contents:

1. Column Layout  
- TYPE  
  • A two‐ or three‐letter code by which the result is referenced in input decks or printouts.  
- Designation  
  • A brief English phrase describing what the code measures.  
- System Applicability  
  • Three sub-columns headed “3D,” “2D,” and “2DSL” (plate/girder).  An asterisk in any of these columns means the quantity is available in that class of model.  
- Load‐Case Number (max/min)  
  • Two integers separated by a slash.  The first is the internal load‐case code under which the maximum value of that quantity is stored, the second is the code for its minimum.

2. Rows (TYPE codes)

- UX  
  • “Average storey displacement in X direction.”  
  • Supported in 3D models (asterisk under 3D).  
  • Load‐case codes: 71 (max) / 72 (min).  

- UY  
  • “Average storey displacement in Y direction.”  
  • Supported in 3D.  
  • Load‐case codes: 73 / 74.  

- UZ  
  • “Average storey displacement in Z direction.”  
  • Supported in 3D.  
  • Load‐case codes: 75 / 76.  

- RZ  
  • “Average storey rotation in the XY‐plane.”  
  • Supported in 3D.  
  • Load‐case codes: 79 / 80.  

- DX  
  • “Inter‐storey drift in X direction” (i.e. differential displacement between two adjacent floors).  
  • Supported in 3D.  
  • Load‐case codes: 81 / 82.  

- DY  
  • “Inter‐storey drift in Y direction.”  
  • Supported in 3D.  
  • Load‐case codes: 83 / 84.  

- DR  
  • “Inter‐storey rotation in the XY‐plane.”  
  • Supported in 3D.  
  • Load‐case codes: 87 / 88.  

3. Context & Usage Notes  
- These outputs are produced only when the superposition type is set to “SLVL” (storey level) via ETYP SLVL.  
- Under the hood, the program first computes all nodal displacements, rotations, support reactions, etc., for each contributing load case, then combines them according to the seismic combination rules.  
- The table’s load‐case numbers serve two purposes: driving the internal storage of maxima/minima and labeling the printed result blocks in the ECHO FACT or ECHO STORY lists.  
- If a quantity is not supported in 2D or plate/girder models, its corresponding columns are left blank (no asterisk). In this excerpt all of the above are currently flagged only for 3D systems.

By consulting this table, a user can select precisely which story‐level seismic result (displacement, drift or rotation) they wish to extract—and know exactly which internal case numbers to reference when reviewing the final combined output.

metadata.sections: 3.11.1 Input Possibilities for Element Types and Scalar Variable

In combination with the basic load case number BASE in record COMB and the storage load case number LC three possibilities are available, with which one can define the load case numbers that are to be used:
