The image depicts a rectangular beam cross section with its centroidal axes and the standard set of named cross-section points used in the AQUA/SELE and MAXIMA modules. It is drawn as a tall, narrow rectangle filled in dark gray and outlined in white. Through its exact geometric center run two perpendicular black lines:  
• A vertical axis (Z)  
• A horizontal axis (Y)  

Each axis extends just beyond the rectangle and terminates in an arrowhead, showing the positive and negative directions used in the software conventions:  
- The horizontal axis arrow on the left is labeled “Y+,” indicating that positive Y points to the left; the arrow on the right is labeled “Y–,” indicating negative Y to the right.  
- The vertical axis arrow at the bottom is labeled “Z+,” indicating positive Z downward; the arrow at the top is labeled “Z–,” indicating negative Z upward.  

Around the perimeter of the rectangle, eight nominal “cross section points” are marked by text labels (no physical dots or markers) to identify the four edge-centers and four corners, as follows:  
1. Top edge center: “Z–”  
2. Bottom edge center: “Z+”  
3. Left edge center: “Y+”  
4. Right edge center: “Y–”  

Corner points (combining Y and Z signs) occupy each vertex:  
• Top-left corner: “Y+Z–”  
• Top-right corner: “Y–Z–”  
• Bottom-right corner: “Y–Z+”  
• Bottom-left corner: “Y+Z+”  

These names correspond to the quadrant‐based cross-section point labels in the AQUA record SPT (or SUPP) entry for SELE, allowing the user to request superposition of internal forces and moments (normal stress “SIG” or shear stress “TAU”) at exactly these locations. By defining points such as Y+Z+, Y–Z+, Y–Z–, Y+Z– and the four midpoints Y+, Y–, Z+, Z–, MAXIMA can select the extremal stress or shear cases (MAX-SIG, MIN-SIG, MAX-TAU, MIN-TAU) for reporting.  

Beneath the drawing is the caption “Figure 3.9: Cross section points,” reinforcing that this schematic is the canonical reference for locating analysis points on a rectangular or steel‐profile beam section inside the RSTAB/PROF/AQUA workflow.

sections: 3.11.4 Input of Cross Section Points for Beams

content:
For beams it is also possible to use for SELE a cross section point defined in program AQUA with record SPT or the designations Y+, Y-, Z+, Z- as well as Y+Z+, Y-Z+, Y-Z-, Y+Z- for the corners and the edge centres of the encasing rectangle (for rectangular cross section and steel profiles from program AQUA record PROF):
 Y+Z+ - corner point in the Ist quadrant
 Y-Z+ - corner point in the IInd quadrant
 Y-Z- - corner point in the IIIrd quadrant
 Y+Z- - corner point in the IVth quadrant
 Y+
 - intersection point positive y axis with the outer edge
 Y-
 - intersection point negative y axis with the outer edge
 Z+
 - intersection point positive z axis with the outer edge
 Z- - intersection point negative z axis with the outer edge
 In the case of the corners and the edge centres of the encasing rectangle an input in the program AQUA record SPT can be omitted.
 The definition of the cross section point is necessary for a superposition with the scalar vari- ables normal stress in cross section point (TYPE SIG) and shear stress in cross section point (TYPE TAU). MAXIMA superimposes here only internal forces and moments. That means, that these internal forces and moments which fulfil the superposition criterion MAX-SIG, MIN-SIG, MAX-TAU or MIN-TAU for the corresponding cross section point are determined.
 If TYPE SIG or TAU is defined for some cross section points within one MAXIMA block, the resultant load case numbers are increased about 1.
 The cross section points can also be defined separated by commas in a record SUPP accord- ing to the rules CADINP, e.g.
 SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE SIG SELE Z+,Y+Z+,Y-Z+,Z-,Y+Z-,Y-Z- LC 3101

content:
In special cases it can be necessary to generate a combination of different superposition values in one result load case. This can be for example a foundation check, where the combination of the minimum vertical load and the maximum horizontal load is very important. The resultant shear force of plates can be also from interest and can be generated with the shear forces v-x and v-y. The user has the possibility to form a reasonable combination of superposition values by using a objective function.
 A objective function is generated with superposition values (described above at TYPE) and perhaps with factors or defined variables (LET or STO variables). An objective function for example for the resultant shear force of a plate reads as follows:
 SUPP COMB 1 EXTR mami ETYP quad TYPE 'SQR(VX**2+VY**2)' LC 101
 Using the objective function, then some rules are to be considered:
 • The superposition values are to be combined reasonably. Only the superposition values of one element type ETYP are to be defined.
 • The rules for CADINP are valid. An objective function should be input with quotation marks ’...’. Blanks are avoid.
 • The result load case number of a superposition with an objective function has to be input manually.
 The determination of an superposition result with an objective function runs exactly with a linear function. For a quadratic function it is to be noted that following relationship is valid
 ( + y)2 > 2 + y2
 If a factor which is defined either explicitly or with a variable is input, it is to be noted that the factor is used only for the weighting during processing of the objective function. This factor does not come in into the numerical value of the superposition result! As an use for that the determination of the boundary stresses is mentioned.
 The user is even responsible for the superposition with an objective function. The user should check the superposition here! With the input of LOAD and FACT in record ECHO all the defined and determined factors and the used load cases are output for every individual superposition value. Only the relevant superposition values are printed with all involved factors, if ECHO CHCK is input.

The user is even responsible for the superposition with an objective function. The user should check the superposition here! With the input of LOAD and FACT in record ECHO all the defined and determined factors and the used load cases are output for every individual superposition value. Only the relevant superposition values are printed with all involved factors, if ECHO CHCK is input..
 Possibilities of an input of an objective function are subsequently described here:
 SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP node TYPE 'PX+PY' LC 5101
 describes as objective function an addition of the support reactions PX and PY.
 The Definition of the variable STO#fact 2.5 and
 SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP node TYPE '#(fact,2.1)*PX+PY' LC 5101
 describe as objective function an addition of the support reactions PX and Py where PX is
 used with a 2.5-times weighting. The input #(fact,2.1) has the effect that the CADINP variable is used with maximal two digits before and one digit behind the ., therefore with 2.5. If only #fact is input, then the value of the variable is rounded off on 3, because CADINP used so only integer values. It is also possible to input the factor 2.5 directly into the objective function:
 SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP node TYPE '2.5*PX+PY' LC 5101

Result sets are used for grouping and for common evaluation of results. They are defined in program SOFiMSHA with RSET. In MAXIMA it is possible to determine the relevant values for a result value. These are for example support reactions in several points and spring forces in different directions.
 For evaluation the literal RSET has to be input at ETYP, the respective ID of the single elements at TYPE and the respective ID of the set (header in SOFiMSHA) at FROM. The ID of the set (header in SOFiMSHA) and the respective single elements can be a number or a literal. It is to be considered that an ID, which is defined as a number, can be input with or without apostrophes both in the program SOFiMSHA and in MAXIMA. The input has to be identical in both programs.
 The results sets have to be input separately. Several result sets can be also defined as a CADINP loop. An input for TO is not allowed.
 The result load case number of a superposition with a results set has to be input manually. It should be noted here, that different result load case numbers have to be defined for different RSET.
 Example: Definition of a RSET for spring forces
 In the example which is shown below the ID of the set is the number 2 and it is input in MAXIMA at SUPP ... FROM. The IDs of the single sets are here ’PVER’ and ’PAXI’.
 PROG SOFIMSHA HEAD ... RSET ID '2' TITL 'Bearing type 2' RSET ID 'PAXI' NO 1002 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'longitudinal' RSET ID 'PVER' NO 1003 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'transverse' ... END
 PROG MAXIMA
 HEAD ECHO RSET FULL COMB ... ... SUPP COMB EXTR ETYP TYPE FROM LC TITL='Bearing type 2' 1 MAMI RSET 'PVER' '2' 2000

RSET ID '2' TITL 'Bearing type 2' RSET ID 'PAXI' NO 1002 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'longitudinal' RSET ID 'PVER' NO 1003 SET SPRI\_RES P TITL 'transverse' ... END. PROG MAXIMA. HEAD ECHO RSET FULL COMB ... ... SUPP COMB EXTR ETYP TYPE FROM LC TITL='Bearing type 2' 1 MAMI RSET 'PVER' '2' 2000.
 1 MAMI RSET 'PAXI' '2' 2010
 END
 Special Feature for Bearing Forces in Bridge Design
 The bearings of a superstructure are created with springs. Then results sets (RSET) are gener- ated for these springs in order to determine the relevant bearing values with the corresponding values of the other bearing axes after calaculation.
 If more results sets (RSET) exist with the same result values, only the ID of one RSET has to be input at FROM. Then the result values of all RSET are always superimposed and the corresponding other values of the result sets are saved in the same corresponing load cases.
 Example for the definition of the result sets (RSET) in SOFiMSHA:
 #define RSET
 RSET ID 'PX' SET SPRI ITEM P NO #start+0 TITL 'PX' RSET ID 'PY' SET SPRI ITEM P NO #start+1 TITL 'PY' RSET ID 'PZ' SET SPRI ITEM P NO #start+2 TITL 'PZ' #enddef
 let#start 200101 RSET ID 'L10L' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 10 left' #include RSET
 let#start 200101
 let#start 200107
 let#start 200107
 RSET ID 'L10R' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 10 right'
 #include RSET
 let#start 200201 RSET ID 'L20L' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 20 left' #include RSET
 let#start 200207
 RSET ID 'L20R' TITL 'Springs bearing axis 20 right'
 #include RSET
 Four result sets L10L, L10R, L20L and L20R are available with their respective result values PX,PY and PZ for the spring force.
 With the following MAXIMA definition these result values of all four result sets are superim- posed although only L10L is input at FROM.

Four result sets L10L, L10R, L20L and L20R are available with their respective result values PX,PY and PZ for the spring force.. With the following MAXIMA definition these result values of all four result sets are superim- posed although only L10L is input at FROM..
 SUPP
 ETYP
 TYPE
 LC
 EXTR=MAMI COMB=11
 FROM
 'RSET' 'PX' 81001 'L10L' 'RSET' 'PY' 81003 'L10R' 'RSET' 'PZ' 81005 'L10R'

With FROM, TO and INC it is possible to control the output of structural elements, groups or individual elements. This is useful for instance, if superposition results should be checked with random samples for all the used load cases and factors (ECHO LOAD,FACT). In a first internal calculation MAXIMA determines the superposition results of all elements. In a second calculation only the selected elements are considered. Only the selected elements are printed then.
 Selection of structural elements:
 Results of elements can be also printed in dependence on the selected structural element. In this case the literals SLN or SAR have to be choosen at FROM. The number of the structural element can then be defined at TO. An input at INC has here no effect. A selection of structural areas is not possible for nodal results. A selection of structural lines is not possible for results of design elements.
 Group selection:
 Results of elements can be also printed groupwise. In this case the literal GRP has to be choosen at FROM. The group number or the name of a secondary group can then be defined at TO. An input at INC has here no effect.
 A group selection is not possible for nodal results. If the internal forces and moments in the nodes of plane and volume elements (ETYP QNOD, BNOD) should be printed groupwise, the group number has to be defined at SELE.
 Element selection:
 If an element selection is desired, then the element or node numbers can be input at FROM and TO whereat INC defines the increment. In the case of an input of only an element or node number at FROM only the superpositon result of this number is printed.
 Selection of a specific tower for the storey results:
 For the storey results it is possible to select only a specific tower for the output of the results with FROM ’TOWR’ and the corresponding ID.
 Without an input at FROM, TO and INC and with a corresponding ECHO option (e.g. ECHO FACT, ECHO QUAD, ECHO BEAM) the results for all elements or nodes are printed which are available.

The table below defines the three input fields you must supply when you invoke the SUM-record to compute a summed superposition for a standard combination (COMB … EXTR STAN).  SUM is specifically designed to take the results of a set of permanent load cases (TYPE PERM) that have been collected under one standard combination rule, multiply each by its user-defined factor, add them up, and store the final superposition result in a single load case.  Once the sum is computed, the COMB rule itself is deleted and only the numerical superposition remains in the database.

Item      | Description                                        | Unit  | Default  
--------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------  
COMB      | Number of the combination rule (must be an EXTR STAN combination)  
          | — identifies which COMB … TYPE PERM entries to sum  | –     | 1       
LC        | Load case number that will receive the summed result  
          | — this single LC will store all superposition outputs | –     | ! (required)  
TITL      | Designation of the new superposition load case      | Lit32 | –       

Detailed Breakdown

1. COMB (Combination Rule Number)  
   • Purpose: Selects one existing standard combination defined by “COMB n EXTR STAN.”  
   • Constraints:  
     – Only combinations of type EXTR STAN (standard combinations with extreme value rules) are permitted.  
     – All initial load cases referenced under that COMB must have TYPE PERM (permanent) and explicit FACTORs.  
   • Default: 1 (if you omit COMB, rule number 1 is assumed).

2. LC (Resulting Load Case Number)  
   • Purpose: Specifies the single load case into which SUM will write the superposed results.  
   • Constraints:  
     – Exactly one LC may be defined for any SUM invocation.  
     – You may not supply a BASE number for COMB when using SUM (BASE can only be 0).  
     – The placeholder “!” in the default column indicates this field is mandatory.  
   • Behavior: After execution, all section results, nodal displacements, forces, etc., from the specified COMB are summed here.

3. TITL (Title/Designation)  
   • Purpose: A text label identifying the new superposition load case.  
   • Format: Lit32 means you have up to 32 characters in total, but only 28 are available for your input, because 4 characters are reserved automatically to prepend a marker (e.g. “SUM_”).  
   • Default: no default title; if omitted, the system will generate a generic designation based on the COMB number.

Cross-References and Output Options  
• See also ECHO: By default TABU YES is used to suppress detailed tabular output. If you want expanded listings of load-case factors, deflections, moments, etc., you must additionally specify either ECHO FULL FULL or ECHO LOAD,FACT.  
• CTRl & COMB: SUM cannot be used in parallel with record SUPP.  As soon as SUM finishes, its parent COMB entry is erased.  
• LC & BASE: SUM forces BASE 0 in COMB; you cannot sum under a non-zero BASE load case.  

Usage Example  
  COMB 1 EXTR STAN  
    TYPE DESI  
    LC 1 TYPE PERM FACT 1.35  
    LC 2 TYPE PERM FACT 1.50  
    LC 4 TYPE PERM FACT 1.50  
    LC 8 TYPE PERM FACT 1.05  
  SUM  
    COMB 1  
    LC 10  
    TITL "SUM_GEO_LIVE"

In this example, SUM reads combination 1, multiplies load cases 1, 2, 4, 8 by their factors, sums them and writes the result into load case 10, titled “SUM_GEO_LIVE.” All intermediate COMB data are then purged, leaving only LC 10’s superposition in the database.

sections: 3.12 SUM – Definition of Sums for Results

content:
See also: ECHO, CTRL, COMB, LC
 | sum
 Using record SUM, sums of results from individual load cases with manually defined factors can be determined. Therefore, the use of record SUM is only allowed for standard com- binations COMB EXTR STAN and related initial load cases which have to be defined as permanent. All defined initial load cases are always taken into account for the determination of the sum, even if they have a favourable effect.
 Example:
 COMB 1 EXTR STAN TYPE DESI LC 1 TYPE PERM FACT 1.35 LC 2 TYPE PERM FACT 1.5 LC 4 TYPE PERM FACT 1.5 LC 8 TYPE PERM FACT 1.05
 The superposition values are determined automatically for the respective system.
 The combination rule is automatically deleted after calculation of the superposition results. Only the superposition results are stored in the database. Therefore, it is not possible to execute superpositions with record SUPP simultaneously with record SUM for such a special combination.
 For the designation TITL 32 characters are available. The input designation can have, however, only 28 characters, because the program uses automatically 4 characters for an information about the superposition at the beginning of the designation.
 Definition of the load lase number:
 Only one resulting load case can be defined at item LC for a standard combination with de- termination of sums. All superposition results are stored in this load case. It is not allowed to define a base load case number BASE in record COMB for the standard combination (only BASE 0 is possible).
 Output extent:
 In addition to the default TABU YES in record ECHO, the extended output can be additionally selected with ECHO FULL FULL or ECHO LOAD,FACT. A selection of individual elements or the printout of the relevant values is not possible. For this purpose, the output of lists is recommended in the Result Viewer.

Below is a comprehensive, self-contained description of the EXPO record’s parameter table, suitable for ingestion into a RAG-driven vector store. It explains the table’s purpose, each field, its unit, default setting and how these entries tie back to the overall EXPO functionality described in the accompanying text.

1. EXPO Record Overview  
   • Purpose  
     – EXPO is a special export record used to dump “superposition” definitions for nodes and elements from either the in-memory database or an INI file into a MAXIMA-compatible input file.  
     – It is intended primarily for advanced users who need to perform symbolic manipulations in MAXIMA based on the finite-element superposition data.  
   • File Handling  
     – If no filename is provided via the “TO” parameter, EXPO will append data to the last file written or will automatically generate a default file named “<project>_MAX.DAT.”  
     – Only the superposition records (SUPP) created in the most recent MAXIMA block are exported. In practice, when exporting from the SSD environment, this means only the superpositions generated by the last “Superpositioning for Combination Rules” task will be used.  
     – Use the SSD command “Export to DAT” for a streamlined workflow that standardizes this export process.

2. Parameter Table Breakdown  
   The EXPO record accepts three keyword parameters—OPT, TO and PASS—each governing a different aspect of the export. Below is a detailed field-by-field description:

   • OPT (Data to export)  
     – Description: A bitmask or code that specifies which categories of data are exported. Regardless of the mask, any export rules defined in the INI file or the database will always be included. In other words, OPT controls extra or selective data, but mandatory specifications are always honored.  
     – Unit: n/a (abstract integer code)  
     – Default: 63 (decimal)  
       • Interpretation: The value 63 typically corresponds to enabling all optional sub-categories. Users can override this to limit output to specific classes of superpositions or auxiliary tables.

   • TO (Name of a file to write to)  
     – Description: Literal text string that designates the target filename for the MAXIMA input data. When provided, EXPO writes (or appends) to this file. If omitted, the system follows the automatic naming/appending rules outlined above.  
     – Unit: Lit96  
       • “Lit96” indicates a character literal of up to 96 bytes. It must conform to the file-naming conventions of the host operating system and avoid reserved characters.  
     – Default: * (asterisk)  
       • Interpretation: A single asterisk means “no explicit filename.” The export engine then uses the last known file or the default “\<project\>_MAX.DAT.”

   • PASS (Password of database)  
     – Description: If the database requires authentication, this parameter supplies the password credential. On invocation, EXPO uses PASS to open the database session before extracting superposition definitions.  
     – Unit: Lit16  
       • “Lit16” indicates a character literal of up to 16 bytes. It should match the database’s password policy.  
     – Default: – (dash)  
       • Interpretation: A dash means “no password supplied.” If the underlying database mandates a password, omitting PASS or setting it to “–” will result in an authentication error.

3. Recommended Usage Tips  
   • Always verify you have run the “Superpositioning for Combination Rules” task immediately before EXPO, to ensure the latest SUPP records are targeted.  
   • If you plan multiple exports in one session, explicitly set “TO” each time to avoid accidental appends to the wrong file.  
   • For repeatable automation, capture the OPT value that matches your desired export scope and store it in the INI file—this guarantees consistency without manual overrides.  
   • If database security is in place, manage PASS securely (for example, via environment variables or a credentials manager) rather than embedding it in scripts.

This description captures the semantics of each table entry, ties them back to the overarching EXPO workflow, and provides practical recommendations for reliable, reproducible exports to MAXIMA.

EXPO
 With the record EXPO you may export the superposition definitions for nodes and elements in the database or in the INI file to an input file for MAXIMA. This may be useful in special cases.
 If the filename is not specified the data will be appended to the most recently defined file or a file with the name project_MAX.DAT is generated.
 Hint:
 It is to be noted, that only the superpositions (records SUPP) of the last MAXIMA block are considered during the export. That means for the export from the SSD, that only the super- positons of the task Superpositioning for Combination Rules which was calculated at last are used for the export file. It is recommended to use the SSD command ’Export to DAT’.

The table defines the single input item “OPT” (short for “option”) which controls what kinds of results are printed by the SOFiMSHA superposition routines (ECHO).  It is organized into four columns:

 1. Item  
    - Always “OPT” in this table; this is the name of the parameter.  

 2. Description  
    - A human-readable explanation that “OPT” must be followed by exactly one literal (keyword) from the provided list.  
    - Each literal keyword enables a different subset or style of output for load-case combinations and superposition results.  

 3. Unit  
    - Always “LIT,” indicating that the expected value is a literal keyword, not a number or path.  

 4. Default  
    - The default setting, used when the user omits the OPT item.  
    - Only the keyword TABS has a default of “YES”; every other option defaults to “off” (represented by “–”).  

Below is a concise description of each available literal:

  • NO  
     – No printed output. Completely suppresses tables or detail.  

  • TABS  
     – General tables of the combination rules and the generated (resultant) load cases.  
     – Default: YES. This means that unless the user explicitly disables it, TABS output will be printed.  

  • CHCK  
     – Print only the decisive (governing) point after superposition at each element or node.  
     – Typically used for quick checks.  

  • FULL  
     – Full, unfiltered output of all defined combinations and every detail of the superposition.  
     – Overrides the more selective options.  

  • LOAD  
     – Print the values of the initial (used) load cases.  
     – Implied when FULL is used.  

  • FACT  
     – Print the load-case contribution factors (partial safety factors GAMMA, combination coefficients PSI, etc.).  
     – With FACT FULL, all GAMMA and PSI values are shown in detail.  
     – With FACT YES, only nonzero factors are shown.  

  • NODE  
     – Output nodal displacements and forces for each selected node.  

  • BOUN  
     – Output single values (reactions) of boundary elements.  

  • BOUS  
     – Output support sums (total reactions) of boundary elements.  

  • BEAM  
     – Output forces and stresses in beam elements.  

  • DSLN  
     – Output results for design (cross-section‐design) elements.  

  • TRUS  
     – Output internal forces in truss elements.  

  • CABL  
     – Output forces in cable elements.  

  • SPRI  
     – Output forces in spring elements.  

  • CFM  
     – Output forces of kinematic constraints (e.g., multi-point constraints).  

  • QUAD  
     – Output stresses or forces in plane (2D) elements.  

  • QNOD  
     – Output the same quantities for plane elements but organized per node.  

  • BRIC  
     – Output stresses or forces in solid (brick) elements.  

  • BNOD  
     – Output the corresponding nodal values for solid elements.  

  • QBED  
     – Output bedding (support‐soil interaction) values.  

  • BSEC  
     – Output internal sectional forces in beam element sections (BSEC FULL prints even those sections suppressed by default).  

  • RSET  
     – Output stored “result sets” (predefined groups of result quantities).  

  • SLVL  
     – Output story‐level results for seismic design (storey shear, overturning moments, etc.).  

  • SUM  
     – Output an overview (“summary”) of all determined load‐case combinations.  

Usage notes:  
• Only those keywords explicitly enabled (or defaulted to YES) will produce output; unused options generate no output.  
• For complex systems, selective activation (e.g. CHCK on a single element via SUPP-FROM/TO) is recommended to avoid extremely large printouts or long run times.  
• ECHO and OPT can be repeated before each SUPP record to tailor the output granularity on a per-superposition basis.  

In RAG/Vector‐store contexts, this table can be indexed under “ECHO options,” “print control keywords,” or “SOFiMSHA output flags” to support rapid retrieval of usage patterns and default behaviors.

The input table is a concise specification of all “ECHO” output-control options available in a SOFiSTiK/MAXIMA SUPP record.  In practice it lets the user tailor exactly which intermediate and final results are written into the PLB or result files during load‐case superposition.  Below is a breakdown of its structure, its columns and rows, and the way it interacts with other SUPP settings:

1. Table Purpose  
   • Governs the verbosity and scope of printed results during superpositions.  
   • Works in tandem with SUPP, COMB and Result-Set definitions.  
   • Each ECHO sub-command (TABS, FULL, LOAD, FACT, CHCK, BSEC, SUM, RSET) has its own VAL settings.

2. Column Definitions  
   • VAL  
     – The keyword or code you supply to ECHO.<sub-command>.  
   • Value of output option  
     – A brief description of what that VAL setting does.

3. Core VAL Settings (common to all ECHO sub-commands unless otherwise noted)  
   • NO  
     – No printed output for this ECHO command.  
   • YES  
     – Standard (default) output. Prints only the combinations or results actually used in the superposition.  
   • FULL  
     – Extended output. Prints all combinations available in the database, even if not used.  
   • P  
     – “Print forces or stresses” option (only applies to certain sub-commands).  
   • CSAV  
     – “Combination-save” mode: store the factor sets as new combination rules (for ECHO CHCK).  

4. ECHO sub-commands and their special notes  
   • ECHO TABS (default = YES)  
     – Prints the first two tables: selected load cases, their factors, GAMMA/Ψ values, and the generated combinations.  
     – FULL prints every possible combination in the database.  
   • ECHO FULL (identical in name to VAL, but here it is the sub-command)  
     – Forces a “full” printout of initial and superposed load cases.  
   • ECHO LOAD  
     – With “YES” prints the raw values of initial load cases prior to superposition; FULL does the same in more detail.  
   • ECHO FACT (default = FULL)  
     – FULL: lists every partial-safety factor (Γ) and combination coefficient (Ψ) used.  
     – YES: prints only those factors ≠ 0.  
   • ECHO CHCK  
     – Prints only the decisive (governing) point after superposition, analogous to LOAD and FACT.  
     – When used with SUPP FROM/TO/INC element or node selection, only that subset’s results are printed.  
     – If you need more detail for a single element, ECHO LOAD YES is sometimes clearer than CHCK.  
     – CHCK CSAV: saves the actual factor sets for each governing value back into the database as new COMB records (numbered 1–999).  
   • ECHO BSEC FULL  
     – Forces printing of beam-section results even when the main SOFiMSHA settings suppress them.  
   • ECHO SUM YES  
     – Prints an overview summary of all determined load-case combinations.  
   • ECHO RSET YES  
     – Automatically set when you work with result sets; CHCK and LOAD/FACT have no effect.

5. Interaction and Ordering Rules  
   • Any explicit ECHO command must appear before the first SUPP record.  
   • Multiple ECHO records in sequence must each repeat the literal “ECHO” to avoid parser confusion.  
   • To mix LOAD and FACT settings for the same block, specify both ECHO LOAD and ECHO FACT before SUPP.  
   • For very large models, limit FULL or FACT FULL to a small selection (via SUPP FROM/TO) to avoid huge PLB files and long runtimes.

In summary, this table is your master‐switch overview for controlling exactly how much detail the MAXIMA superposition step will print.  By choosing the right combination of ECHO sub-command and VAL, you can quickly verify key results or produce an exhaustive audit trail of every factor, combination, and internal force.

The table shown is a concise summary of three of the most commonly used “output-value” options for the ECHO record in the SOFiSTiK MAXIMA input.  Each row identifies an ECHO sub-option (Item), gives a brief Description of what will be printed when that sub-option is active, and shows that there is no associated Unit or Default value specified in the table itself.  In practice these options are invoked by a statement of the form  
    ECHO VAL <item> YES/FULL  
or, in combination with other ECHO items, to tailor the extent of data written to the PLB (print) file.  

1. Item = V  
   – Description:  
     • Displacements at nodes (global or local, depending on context).  
     • For QUAD (plate or foundation) elements, also prints the foundation stresses (soil contact pressures).  
   – Unit: –  
   – Default: –  
   
   When you include “V” in your ECHO VAL list, the program will output all nodal displacements for the selected load cases or superpositions.  In the special case of foundation (QUAD) elements this flag additionally triggers the display of the computed soil-structure interface stresses.  

2. Item = FULL  
   – Description:  
     • Extensive output, equivalent to combining P + V  
   – Unit: –  
   – Default: –  

   Specifying “FULL” requests a fully detailed printout of both force/stress results (the P-type quantities) and displacement data (the V-type quantities).  This is the most comprehensive single-keyword printout mode and typically produces large volumes of data.  It effectively sets both P and V on in one go.  

3. Item = CSAV  
   – Description:  
     • Only operative in combination with ECHO CHCK (see below)  
   – Unit: –  
   – Default: –  

   The “CSAV” modifier is meaningful only when you are using ECHO CHCK to examine superposition check points or selected element/node ranges.  In that context it instructs SOFiSTiK to save all individual load-case factors that contribute to each decisive result point.  These factor combinations are then stored back into the database as new combination rules (using COMB numbers 1–999).  

How this fits into the broader ECHO framework  
– SUPP defines which elements or nodes the superpositions apply to (FROM/TO/INC).  
– ECHO LOAD YES (or FULL FULL) will print the values of initial load cases before showing superposition results.  
– ECHO FACT YES/FULL controls how much detail you see of the γ (partial safety) and ψ (combination) factors.  
– ECHO CHCK prints only the decisive resultant value after all superposition factors have been applied; with CSAV it also archives the factor sets.  
– ECHO TABS YES (default) prints only the combinations actually used in superpositions; TABS FULL prints the entire database of combinations.  
– If you need beam-section results, add ECHO BSEC FULL.  
– A summary of all determined load-case combinations is obtained with ECHO SUM YES.  
– For very large models, it is recommended to narrow the output to a few critical elements or nodes to avoid huge PLB files and long output times.  

By choosing among V, FULL, and CSAV—and by combining them appropriately with LOAD, FACT, CHCK, TABS, etc.—you can precisely control both the volume and the content of your printout, ensuring that you see exactly the displacement, stress, and factor information you need for verification or reporting.

See also: SUPP
 ECHO
 VAL
 Value of output option
 LT
 *
 NO
 No printed output
 YES
 —
 Regular output
 P
 Output of forces or stresses
 First two tables with the selected load cases including the load case factors as well as the de- fined GAMMA and PSI values and the generated load cases (ECHO TABS YES = default) are printed. Only these combinations which are used for the superpositions are output with ECHO TABS YES. The printout of all combinations which are available in the database is done with ECHO TABS FULL.
 If only the combination rules are defined in a MAXIMA input without definitions for the super- positions (without any record SUPP), it is possible to get the output of the combination rules and the table ’Load case selection and actions’ with the explicit input of ECHO TABS FULL. Then the superposition results are printed, if a corresponding input for ECHO is done explicitly.
 An explicit input for ECHO must be positioned before the record SUPP! Thus the output extent can be modified individually for each superposition. In the case of multiple ECHO records in a row, the record name ECHO has to be repeated for each record in order to avoid confusion of ECHO literals with identical record names.
 The values of the used initial load cases are printed with the explicit input ECHO LOAD YES or with ECHO FULL FULL before those of the superposition load cases.
 The output of the partial safety factors and combination coefficients is controlled via an explicit input of ECHO FACT. With ECHO FACT FULL all involved GAMMA and PSI values of the initial load cases and the factors resulting from these are output in detail. Only the factors unequal to zero are output with ECHO FACT YES. The default for FACT is FULL. Using both items (LOAD and FACT) the user should check the superposition results by investigating random samples!
 The input ECHO CHCK prints only the respective decisive point after the superposition (analo- gous to ECHO LOAD and ECHO FACT). If an element or node selection with SUPP FROM TO INC is used simultaneously with an input ECHO CHCK, then the relevant values only of this selection are printed as superposition result. It can be clearer sometimes to use ECHO LOAD YES for selected elements instead of ECHO CHCK, because only the factors unequal to zero are printed with ECHO LOAD YES.

If an element or node selection with SUPP FROM TO INC is used simultaneously with an input ECHO CHCK, then the relevant values only of this selection are printed as superposition result. It can be clearer sometimes to use ECHO LOAD YES for selected elements instead of ECHO CHCK, because only the factors unequal to zero are printed with ECHO LOAD YES..
 Using the Result Sets an input ECHO CHCK has no influence and ECHO RSET YES is set.
 ECHO CHCK CSAV saves the factors of the load cases for each relevant value as combination rule with the number of the resulting load case into the database. In this case the numbers of the resulting load cases have to be from 1 to 999, because the maximum number of the combination is 999 in the record COMB.
 With the input of ECHO BSEC FULL even the results for beam sections are printed, which should not be printed due to the input in the program SOFiMSHA.
 An overview of the determined load case combinations is requested with ECHO SUM YES.
 Hint
 In the case of big systems with a lot of elements we recommend to check the results with the extensive output only for a special element. This can be done with ECHO CHCK or with a definition of this element in record SUPP item FROM and ECHO LOAD,FACT. If the extensive output e.g. with ECHO FULL FULL is chosen for all elements, this may lead to a longer computational time and to a very large PLB file.

The table summarizes the input fields (records) you must supply to the MAXiMA TRAC command in order to trace back how a given Load Case was generated by superposition.  It is organized into four columns—Item, Description, Unit and Default—and lists six mandatory/sub-optional parameters:  

1.  Item “LC”  
    •  Description: The resulting Load Case number from a previous MAXiMA run that you wish to decompose.  
    •  Unit: none  
    •  Default: (mandatory, no default)  

2.  Item “ETYP” (Element Type)  
    •  Description: Specifies the class of finite-element or result you are tracing.  You enter one literal code (LIT) chosen from:  
       –  NODE: nodal displacements or forces  
       –  SPAC: nodal accelerations & velocities  
       –  BOUN: individual boundary elements  
       –  BOUS: sums of boundary elements  
       –  BEAM: beam elements  
       –  DSLN: design (SIR) elements  
       –  BSCT: external beam sections (output from SIR)  
       –  TRUS: truss elements  
       –  CABL: cable elements  
       –  SPRI: springs  
       –  CFM: kinematic constraints  
       –  QUAD: plane (2D) elements  
       –  QNOD: nodes of plane elements  
       –  QBED: bedding of plane elements  
       –  BRIC: 3D (volume) elements  
       –  BNOD: nodes of volume elements  
       –  RSET: result set identifier  
       –  SLVL: storey‐level results  
    •  Unit: LIT (literal code)  
    •  Default: (mandatory, no default)  

3.  Item “ELEM”  
    •  Description: The specific element or node number you are tracing, or (for result sets) an identifier of the set.  
    •  Unit: none  
    •  Default: (mandatory, no default)  

4.  Item “X”  
    •  Description: For BEAM and DSLN elements only—enter the X-coordinate along the beam axis (or SIR design element axis) where a cross-section result was extracted.  
    •  Unit: metres (m) or non-dimensional depending on model units  
    •  Default: (optional; only required for BEAM/DSLN cross-section results)  

5.  Item “SELE”  
    •  Description:  
       –  For BEAM or DSLN cross-section stresses (SIG/TAU): the stress point index (1–4) within the section.  
       –  For QUAD/BRIC nodal results: a group number identifying a node group (QNOD/BNOD).  
       –  For BOUN elements: the node number at that boundary.  
    •  Unit: integer (– or LIT4 in legacy notation)  
    •  Default: (optional; required only for the types above)  

6.  Item “OPT” (Tracing Options)  
    •  Description: Controls how deeply TRAC will follow the chain of superpositions.  Possible codes:  
       –  I   : trace intermediate (nested) superpositions as well  
       –  IF  : trace only first-level input load cases (default)  
    •  Unit: LIT (literal)  
    •  Default: IF  

Usage notes and context (from the manual):  
•  You invoke TRAC in its own MAXiMA run—cannot be combined with a new superposition in the same execution.  
•  TRAC reads the original SUPP and COMB records for the specified result, then retrieves each input Load Case and its MAXiMA-computed factor.  If that result type is stored in the database, TRAC will re-compute the superposition and compare against the stored value as a check.  On-the-fly results (e.g. beam cross-section stresses or quad Von Mises) cannot be validated.  
•  CSAV can save the discovered input cases & factors into a new combination number.  That combination can later be “copied” into actual loads in SOFiLOAD (using COPY … COMB) and then run through ASE.  Only initial load cases based on real loads will be preserved in CSAV; internally generated or modal/internal-force cases are skipped (with a warning).  
•  Tendon stresses for QUAD elements cannot currently be traced.  
•  Recommended workflow example:  
   –  In MAXIMA:  
     PROG MAXIMA  
     HEAD …  
     TRAC LC 2155 ETYP NODE ELEM 12 OPT IF CSAV 55  
     TRAC LC 2156 ETYP NODE ELEM 12 OPT IF CSAV 56  
     END  
   –  In SOFiLOAD:  
     PROG SOFILOAD  
     HEAD …  
     LC 201 TYPE NONE COPY 55 COMB  
     LC 202 TYPE NONE COPY 56 COMB  
     END  
   –  In ASE:  
     PROG ASE  
     HEAD …  
     LC 201,202  
     END  

This table and associated notes give you all the parameter definitions, units and defaults you need to configure a TRAC run in order to investigate the provenance of any critical load effect identified by MAXiMA superposition.

Below is a field‐by‐field description of the TRAC input record (the “input table”) used by MAXiMA.  This table defines exactly which parameters must be provided to TRACE a given superposed load case, how they relate, their allowed types/values, and any special constraints.  Whenever relevant, pointers to the related SUPP or COMB tables are noted; these are read in by TRAC to reconstruct how a result was generated.

1. Record identifier  
   - Name: PROG  
   - Type: keyword  
   - Values: MAXIMA (for tracing), SOFILOAD (for generating loads), ASE (for final analysis)  
   - Notes: Begins each block: e.g. “PROG MAXIMA … END.”  

2. Header separator  
   - Name: HEAD  
   - Type: keyword  
   - Values: arbitrary text or ellipses (“…”)  
   - Notes: purely cosmetic, no effect on tracing logic  

3. Target Load Case  
   - Name: LC  
   - Type: integer (>0)  
   - Description: the ID of the resulting load case whose superposition you want to trace  

4. Element Context  
   - Name: ETYP  
   - Type: enumeration  
   - Allowed Values:  
     • NODE – trend result at a node (e.g. forces or moments)  
     • ELEM – for stresses or internal forces on elements  
   - Notes: further disambiguated by ELEM and SELE  

5. Element or Node Number  
   - Name: ELEM  
   - Type: integer  
   - Description: the element number (if ETYP=ELEM) or node number (if ETYP=NODE or BOUN)  

6. Beam‐position coordinate (optional)  
   - Name: X  
   - Type: real  
   - Applies when: ETYP refers to a BEAM element  
   - Description: normalized or absolute position along the beam axis where stress/internal‐force is probed  

7. Stress‐point or Group selector  
   - Name: SELE  
   - Type: integer  
   - Semantics:  
     • If the load case is “SIG”/“TAU” on a BEAM cross‐section, SELE specifies which stress point  
     • For QUAD elements: SELE = QNOD group number  
     • For BRIC elements: SELE = BNOD group number  
     • For boundary elements (BOUN): SELE = node number on that boundary  
   - Notes: mirrors exactly the SELE parameter in the SUPP record  

8. Trace‐depth control  
   - Name: OPT  
   - Type: string  
   - Allowed Values:  
     • 'IF' – immediate factors only (stop at first level)  
     • 'DF' – deep/follow full hierarchy of intermediate superpositions  
   - Default/Required: must be explicitly set  

9. Save‐combination number  
   - Name: CSAV  
   - Type: integer  
   - Description: the ID under which the determined input‐load‐case combination will be stored in CDB  
   - Post‐condition: SOFiLOAD COPY COMB record can then read CSAV to generate real loads  

10. End of record  
    - Name: END  
    - Type: keyword  
    - Notes: terminates the MAXIMA block  

Constraints & Special Notes  
• TRAC must run in isolation (cannot co‐exist with a standard superposition call).  
• Tendon stresses for QUAD elements cannot be traced.  
• If the stored result type is in CDB, TRAC validates its recomputed superposition against the stored value. On‐the‐fly results (e.g. beam‐section stresses or quad Von Mises) cannot be validated.  
• Initial load cases containing only internal forces (no “real” loads) are not converted by SOFiLOAD; a warning is issued.  
• Certain superposition types cannot be transformed into loads (difference load cases from CSM, modal/in-elastic internal forces, eigenvalue/time‐step results).  

Workflow Summary  
1. MAXIMA/TRAC reads SUPP and COMB records for the given LC, ETYP, ELEM, SELE.  
2. It resolves (to depth OPT) all input‐load cases and their factors.  
3. If requested, it saves that factor list as a new combination (CSAV).  
4. SOFiLOAD COPY … COMB (using CSAV) generates actual distributed loads in new LC(s).  
5. ASE then analyses the new load case(s).

The input table defines two optional parameters that can be supplied on the TRAC record to control how MAXiMA traces and optionally saves the combination of input load cases and their factors.  Below is a structured description of each parameter, including its purpose, allowed values, units (if any), default behavior, and how it interacts with the wider TRAC → CSAV → SOFiLOAD workflow.

1.  Parameter “F”  
    •  Name  
       –  F (a filter flag)  
    •  Description  
       –  When present, this flag instructs TRAC to omit any input load cases whose factor in the superposition is zero. In other words, if a given load case did not contribute at all to the resulting combined load case, it will not appear in the traced list of inputs.  
       –  This can make the trace output more concise by removing “dead” load cases.  
    •  Allowed Values / Syntax  
       –  Simply include the letter F in the TRAC command line. No assignment or numeric value follows.  
    •  Unit  
       –  none (boolean flag)  
    •  Default  
       –  OFF (i.e. if you do not specify F, all input load cases – including those with zero factor – will be listed)  

2.  Parameter “CSAV”  
    •  Name  
       –  CSAV (save combination)  
    •  Description  
       –  Directs MAXiMA to collect the input load cases and their computed superposition factors into a new “combination” record in the CDB (case database). You must provide a new combination number, in the range 1 … 999.  
       –  Later, SOFiLOAD can read that saved combination—via a COPY … COMB command—and generate a fresh load case (with its own number) that reproduces exactly the same superposed loads. This new load case can then be run again in ASE or any downstream module.  
       –  Internals-Only Warning: CSAV will omit any input load case that was not based on a “real” initial load (for instance, results from modal superposition, tendon stresses for QUAD elements, eigenvalue analyses, step‐by‐step time methods, etc.). SOFiLOAD will generate a warning if it detects such cases.  
    •  Allowed Values / Syntax  
       –  CSAV nnn, where nnn is an integer 1–999.  
       –  Example: “CSAV 55” in the TRAC command header.  
    •  Unit  
       –  none (integer identifier)  
    •  Default  
       –  none (if you omit CSAV, no new combination is stored; TRAC only writes output to the console, with no saved combination)  

Additional Notes on Workflow Integration  
•  Typical TRAC invocation:  
     PROG MAXIMA  
     HEAD …  
       TRAC LC 2155 ETYP NODE ELEM 12 OPT 'IF' F CSAV 55  
       TRAC LC 2156 ETYP NODE ELEM 12 OPT 'IF' CSAV 56  
     END  

•  After TRAC with CSAV has executed, you will have two new combination records (e.g. #55 and #56) in CDB. To convert those saved combinations into actual load cases that ASE can digest, use SOFiLOAD:  
     PROG SOFILOAD  
     HEAD …  
       LC 201 TYPE NONE COPY 55 COMB  
       LC 202 TYPE NONE COPY 56 COMB  
     END  

•  Finally, run ASE on the newly created load cases:  
     PROG ASE  
     HEAD …  
       LC 201,202  
     END  

By understanding and employing “F” and “CSAV” in concert, you can (1) prune away non-contributing load cases from your trace output for clarity, and (2) persist the exact combination of load cases/factors into a reusable combination that can be re-loaded, re-computed, or further analyzed in downstream programs.

 TRAC
 With the use of command TRAC, it is possible to trace a Combination and retrieve detailed information on how a resulting Load Case has been generated, as an outcome of a MAXiMA superposition. More specifically, this feature will discover and print out all the input Load Cases, associated with a Combination, with their corresponding factors, that have been determined by MAXiMA. This is especially useful in order to investigate, after a superposition has been performed, how a critical Load Case on a specific element has been generated.
 The required input parameters are the number of the resulting Load Case of interest, as well as the element type and number. For BEAM elements, X position must be specified too, and, in case a Load Case refers to cross section stresses (SIG / TAU), a stress point must be entered in parameter SELE, analogously to the corresponding parameters of SUPP record. Parameter SELE may be also used to specify a group number for nodes on QUAD or BRIC elements (QNOD / BNOD). For boundary elements (BOUN) a node number has to be input for the relevant boundary with SELE. Finally, with parameter OPT it is possible to control the depth of the tracing, ie. if intermediate superpositions should be resolved too or tracing should stop on the first level of detected input Load Cases.
 Using the above parameters, the corresponding SUPP and COMB information, which were originally used during the superposition that generated the specified Load Case, will be initially read from the database. With this information available, it is subsequently possible to retrieve the associated input Load Cases, with their corresponding factors that have been used in the superposition. In case the detected result type is stored in the database, as is in most circumstances, TRAC will attempt to validate that the superposition result computed during tracing matches to what has been actually stored in CDB, during the superposition. However, in case of result types computed on-the-fly, such as stresses on stress points of BEAM’s cross sections, or Von Mises stresses for QUAD elements, this is not possible.

In case the detected result type is stored in the database, as is in most circumstances, TRAC will attempt to validate that the superposition result computed during tracing matches to what has been actually stored in CDB, during the superposition. However, in case of result types computed on-the-fly, such as stresses on stress points of BEAM’s cross sections, or Von Mises stresses for QUAD elements, this is not possible..
 Hint
 Tracing must be performed in an individual MAXiMA run, as it cannot co-exist with the standard superposition functionality.
 Currently it is not possible to trace superpositions associated with Tendon Stresses for Quad Elements.
 The determined load cases and their factors are save in a new load case combination with the input of a combination number for CSAV. Afterward the loads for a new load case can be generated with the saved combination factors in the program SOFiLOAD. For this the combina- tion number and the combination type COMB have to be input in record COPY of the program SOFiLOAD. This new load case can still be used e.g. in a calculation with the program ASE.
 The transformation of load cases which are saved with CSAV into loads with SOFiLOAD is only possible for initial load cases which contain ’real’ loads. Initial load cases whose internal forces or other results are used in the superposition and which are not based on ’real’ loads are not considered whilst saving of the new combination. They get a warning in the program SOFiLOAD.
 Following superposition results can not transformed into loads:
 • Difference load cases from CSM construction stage (consideration in ASE with group control)
 Internal forces from modal analyses (workflow earthquake)
 • Results from calculation of eigenvalues
 • Results from calculation with time-step-method
 The results of CSAV should be checked if a group control was used.. It is recommended to used CSAV only in the case of the consideration of all groups in the previous calculation and superposition.

For the user of SSD it is possible to define the superposition inputs interactive.
 In the SSD there is the task Combination Rules on the one hand and to the second the task Superpositioning for Combination Rules.
 The task Combination Rules define the superposition kind.
 With the task Superpositioning for Combination Rules the user defines which maximum and/or minimum values of a specific scalar variable for an element type which is to be input should be determined. The quantity of output can be specified additionally.
 The input possibilities depend on the design code and the static system which were selected at the beginning of the input process.
 For the combinations and superposition a reasonable default is generated from the information of the database according to the used design code (INI file).
 The Name of combinations and superpositions is generated automatically. However, it is pos- sible to modify this definition according to the user requests. Here is to be considered, that the preset Name begins with a blank. This blank must be deleted for manual modifications, because otherwise the program sets the default again.

The definition of the combinations with the respective actions and the relevant load cases is done in the task Combination Rules. The input of the actions is not necessary for superposi- tions without actions (e.g. according to German DIN 1045 old).

The two-column table at the bottom of your input defines the default mapping between “Superposition kind” (i.e. the combination rule you choose) and the “Type of resulting loadcases” that will be assigned automatically when you perform a simplified superposition (for example under German DIN 18800 or Austrian ÖNORM B 4300). In the MAXIMA input this corresponds to setting the COMB record’s Superposition Kind and the TYPE record’s load-case classification. Below is a breakdown of its structure, content and intended use:

1. Table Structure  
   • Column 1: Superposition kind  
     – Lists the name of the predefined, simplified superposition rule. These rules determine which combination coefficients and safety factors apply.  
   • Column 2: Type of resulting loadcases  
     – Specifies how the newly generated loadcases will be classified (in terms of ULS or SLS, fundamental or accidental, characteristic or frequent, etc.). This classification is stored in the TYPE record of each result loadcase.  

2. Purpose & Context  
   • When you select one of the simplified combination rules in the Superposition Manager, the software must also tag every generated loadcase with an appropriate “type.”  
   • This type is used later for filtering, reporting and ensuring that each result is interpreted under the correct limit‐state criteria (ultimate vs. serviceability, accidental vs. fundamental, characteristic vs. frequent, etc.).  
   • For fully general or user-defined combinations (COMB EXPL) you must assign types manually or leave them untyped; this table only applies to the preset simplified rules.

3. Row-by-Row Description  
   Row 1  
     • Superposition kind: “ULS fundamental simplified”  
       – A streamlined ultimate‐limit‐state combination rule (e.g. per DIN 18800).  
     • Type of resulting loadcases: “ULS fundamental combination”  
       – All result loadcases created under this rule are tagged as fundamental ULS combinations.  
   Row 2  
     • Superposition kind: “ULS accidental simplified”  
       – A simplified accidental ultimate‐limit‐state rule (applicable only in those national codes that define such a case).  
     • Type of resulting loadcases: “ULS accidental combination”  
       – Result loadcases receive the accidental ULS classification.  
   Row 3  
     • Superposition kind: “SLS charact. (rare) simplified”  
       – A reduced‐complexity, rare‐event serviceability‐limit‐state rule (the characteristic serviceability combination).  
     • Type of resulting loadcases: “SLS characteristic combination”  
       – Loadcases generated through this rule are labeled as characteristic SLS combinations.

4. How It Fits into the Workflow  
   • After choosing the “Superposition kind” in the COMB record, the software automatically picks the “Type of resulting loadcases” from this table if you are using a simplified code.  
   • If you switch to a full EN-199x rule set or to an explicitly defined combination, other default mappings or manual assignments apply.  
   • You do not need to enter the TYPE record manually for these three simplified rules—the mapping is built in.

5. Recommendations  
   • Always verify that the chosen Superposition kind matches the design code you intend to use (e.g. make sure “ULS fundamental simplified” is only used under its applicable national code).  
   • For more complex or user-specified load combinations, explicitly review and, if necessary, override the automatically assigned TYPE fields in the result loadcases to ensure they align with your project’s limit‐state classification scheme.

Interpretation in context of combination definitions:  
This view is where the user assigns one or more “actions” (e.g. self-weight, live-load in offices labeled here “Pay load offices”) to a superposition combination. For each action, the partial safety factors (γ-values) and combination coefficients (ψ-values) can be overridden on a per-combination basis by checking the box and editing the value. The “Select Loadcases” (“<<”) button is used to pick which load-case entries from the database belong under the highlighted action. Finally, “Select Rule” and “Define Rule” let the user choose between a standard superposition (STAN), non-linear extrema (NONL), explicit combination (EXPL) or one of the EN/DIN-based ULS/SLS presets, according to the loaded design code.
